#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
rimbridge_client.py - talk to a LIVE RimWorld through the RimBridgeServer GABP bridge.

*** THIS DRIVES A RUNNING GAME. THERE IS NO UNDO. ***
=====================================================
Every call goes straight into the RimWorld process that is on screen right now.
A colony that took twenty minutes to load can be wrecked by one careless call.
This module deliberately does NOT enforce read-only - it cannot, because the
bridge decides what a tool does, not us - so the discipline is yours:

  SAFE   rimbridge/ping, get_bridge_status, list_capabilities, list_logs,
         rimworld/get_game_info, list_*, get_*, search_debug_actions
  NEVER  rimworld/execute_debug_action, spawn_thing, save_game, load_game,
         set_*, rimbridge/run_lua, run_script - these mutate or destroy state

Searching for and DESCRIBING a debug action is free. EXECUTING one is not.

READ-ONLY IS NOT THE SAME AS HARMLESS
=====================================
2026-08-10: `rimworld/list_debug_action_roots` and `rimworld/search_debug_actions`
killed a live 562-mod colony. Neither tool changes game state - both build
RimWorld's debug node graph on the main thread, and on a load order this size
that build never returned. Unity stopped pumping, Windows raised AppHangB1, and
the process was terminated ~4 minutes later; 23 minutes of load time went with
it. There was no exception in Player.log, just silence.

So: on a heavily modded install, treat the four `*_debug_action*` discovery
tools as dangerous, not as reads. If you must call them, save the game first,
give them a multi-minute timeout, and expect that a timeout means the game is
already gone rather than merely slow. Everything else in the safe list above
returned in 7-15ms on that same install.

WHY THIS EXISTS
===============
The bridge is only reachable while the game is up, and the token changes on
every launch, so anything hardcoded is stale within one restart. This module
scrapes the live token out of Player.log so a session never starts with a
paste-the-token step that silently uses last launch's value and then fails with
a bare "Invalid authentication token".

WIRE FORMAT (derived from the shipped assemblies, not guessed)
==============================================================
Transport is raw TCP on 127.0.0.1 with LSP-style header framing. Everything
below was read out of the metadata/#US heaps of the DLLs RimWorld actually
loaded, at
  <Workshop>/294100/3727949765/1.6/Assemblies/{Lib.GAB.dll, Gabp.Runtime.dll}

  * Lib.GAB.dll #US heap: "Content-Length: {0}", "Content-Type: application/json",
    "\r\n\r\n"  ->  headers, blank line, then a UTF-8 JSON body of exactly
    Content-Length bytes. Reader prefix literal is "Content-Length:".
  * Gabp.Runtime.dll custom-attribute blob (JsonProperty names, in declaration
    order): v, id, type, method, params, result, error  ->  the request/response
    envelope. Events use: v, id, type, channel, seq, payload.
  * Lib.GAB.dll #US heap: "gabp/1" (envelope v), "request"/"response"/"event"
    (envelope type), and the method names "session/hello", "tools/list",
    "tools/call", "events/subscribe", "events/unsubscribe", "attention/current",
    "attention/ack".
  * Gabp.Runtime.dll blob, session/hello params: token, bridgeVersion, platform,
    launchId, clientInfo{name, version, author}. Welcome result: agentId, app,
    capabilities, schemaVersion, serverInfo{name, version}.
  * tools/call params: {name, arguments}. tools/list result: {tools:[...]}.
  * Server rejects anything before the handshake with "Session not established.
    Send session/hello first." and a bad token with "Invalid authentication
    token" (Lib.GAB.dll #US heap).

Tool names are canonical GABP form ^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]*(/[a-z][a-z0-9_-]*)+$ -
"rimworld/get_game_info", never the dotted MCP adapter spelling
"rimworld.get_game_info". Lib.GAB rejects the dotted form outright.

USAGE
=====
    python rimbridge_client.py --list-tools
    python rimbridge_client.py --call rimbridge/get_bridge_status
    python rimbridge_client.py --call rimworld/search_debug_actions \
        --json '{"query": "pawn", "limit": 50}'

    from rimbridge_client import RimBridge, discover_from_log
    host, port, token = discover_from_log()
    with RimBridge(host, port, token) as rb:
        print(rb.call("rimbridge/ping"))

Host/port/token resolve in this order: CLI flag, then environment
(RIMBRIDGE_HOST / GABP_SERVER_PORT / GABP_TOKEN - the same names Lib.GAB reads),
then the newest pair scraped from Player.log, then the built-in defaults.

Dependency-free: Python 3.8+ stdlib only. Keep it that way.
"""

import sys as _rm_sys, pathlib as _rm_pl  # noqa: E401
_rm_sys.path.insert(0, str(_rm_pl.Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3] / "src" / "RimMandrake" / "Utils"))
from rmpaths import rm_path, rm_str, rm_win  # noqa: E402,F401  (data root: rmpaths.py)
import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import os
import re
import socket
import sys
import time
import uuid

__all__ = ["RimBridge", "RimBridgeError", "discover_from_log", "DEFAULT_PLAYER_LOG"]

DEFAULT_HOST = "127.0.0.1"
DEFAULT_PORT = 5174
DEFAULT_TOKEN = ""

DEFAULT_PLAYER_LOG = os.path.join(
    os.path.expanduser("~"), "AppData", "LocalLow", "Ludeon Studios",
    "RimWorld by Ludeon Studios", "Player.log")

# Under WSL, expanduser("~") is /home/<user>, so DEFAULT_PLAYER_LOG points at a
# Linux path that will never exist and discovery silently finds nothing. The
# symptom is "no bridge token in Player.log - is RimWorld up?" while the token
# is sitting in the real log and the game is running perfectly.
#
# ⚠️ Finding the log does NOT make WSL work. RimBridge binds Windows loopback
# and WSL2 is NAT-mode, so the socket is refused regardless. The fallback exists
# so the error you get is the TRUE one (connection refused, wrong interpreter)
# instead of a false one that sends you looking at the game. Reported by a retired seat,
# 2026-08-12, after it cost them the hunt twice.
WSL = sys.platform.startswith("linux") and os.path.isdir("/mnt/c")

# ADHOC_BRIDGE_CALL_LOG_1: every session (connect -> close) appends one row here so
# northstar_driver/bridge_utilization.py can count ad-hoc python.exe scripts as ACTIVE
# bridge time. Outside git (a program reads it). RIMBRIDGE_SESSION_LOG overrides; "" disables.
# The default is resolved only when the variable is unset: a .get() default runs eagerly, so a caller that set it
# (a selftest with "") still died on RmDataRootUnset with no data root configured.
SESSION_LOG = (os.environ["RIMBRIDGE_SESSION_LOG"] if "RIMBRIDGE_SESSION_LOG" in os.environ
               else rm_win("scratch", "bridge_sessions.jsonl") if os.name == "nt"
               else rm_str("scratch", "bridge_sessions.jsonl"))


def _log_session(started, calls, client):
    """Best effort: a logging failure must never break a bridge script."""
    if not SESSION_LOG or started is None:
        return
    try:
        row = {"started": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", time.gmtime(started)),
               "finished": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", time.gmtime()),
               "seconds": round(time.time() - started, 3), "calls": calls, "client": client,
               "script": os.path.basename(sys.argv[0]) if sys.argv else ""}
        with open(SESSION_LOG, "a", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            fh.write(json.dumps(row) + "\n")
    except Exception:
        pass


# BRIDGE_CALL_EVIDENCE_WIRE_LOST_REPLY_UNKNOWN (2026-10-10): EVERY tools/call through this client - runners and
# ad-hoc scripts alike - appends a `start` row before sending and an `end` row after (ok / error / lost /
# INDETERMINATE) to a bounded JSONL. A MUTATING call (anything failing looks_read_only) also leaves an in-flight
# marker that is removed only when the bridge ANSWERS. If the reply is lost (timeout, closed socket, crash) the marker
# stays as INDETERMINATE and every later mutating call - the retry included - raises IndeterminateError until
# `python rimbridge_client.py --reconcile` records what actually happened (read the game with read-only calls
# first). If the intent row cannot be written, the mutation is refused; a read only warns.
# Default on Windows only: the bridge is reachable only from python.exe (WSL2 is NAT-mode, so a WSL call dies at
# connect, before any tools/call), and a WSL selftest faking a lost reply must never leave a REAL marker behind.
EVIDENCE_LOG = (os.environ["RIMBRIDGE_EVIDENCE_LOG"] if "RIMBRIDGE_EVIDENCE_LOG" in os.environ   # lazy: SESSION_LOG
                else rm_win("scratch", "bridge_calls.jsonl") if os.name == "nt" else "")
EVIDENCE_MAX_BYTES = 20 * 1024 * 1024
_RUN_ID = uuid.uuid4().hex[:12]
_ACTIVE = set()                       # cids in flight in THIS process


class IndeterminateError(RuntimeError):
    """A previous mutating call's outcome is unknown; refusing further mutations until reconciled."""


def _ev_now():
    return time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", time.gmtime())


def _inflight_dir():
    return os.path.join(os.path.dirname(EVIDENCE_LOG) or ".", "bridge_inflight")


def _evidence(row, required=False):
    """Append one row; rotate past EVIDENCE_MAX_BYTES. required=True raises OSError instead of swallowing it."""
    if not EVIDENCE_LOG:
        return
    try:
        d = os.path.dirname(EVIDENCE_LOG)
        if d:
            os.makedirs(d, exist_ok=True)
        try:
            if os.path.getsize(EVIDENCE_LOG) > EVIDENCE_MAX_BYTES:
                os.replace(EVIDENCE_LOG, EVIDENCE_LOG + ".1")
        except OSError:
            pass
        with open(EVIDENCE_LOG, "a", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            fh.write(json.dumps(row, sort_keys=True) + "\n")
    except OSError:
        if required:
            raise
        print("[rimbridge_client] evidence row NOT written to %s" % EVIDENCE_LOG, file=sys.stderr)


def _inflight_write(rec):
    if not EVIDENCE_LOG:
        return
    os.makedirs(_inflight_dir(), exist_ok=True)
    p = os.path.join(_inflight_dir(), "%s.json" % rec["cid"])
    tmp = p + ".tmp"
    with open(tmp, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        json.dump(rec, fh)
    os.replace(tmp, p)


def _inflight_clear(cid):
    # Windows refuses to delete a file another process holds open, and every concurrent client's
    # outstanding_indeterminate() opens every marker: one failed remove strands a marker that turns UNKNOWN once this
    # process exits and refuses every later mutating call (pass 8, 2026-10-13). Retry briefly.
    p = os.path.join(_inflight_dir(), "%s.json" % cid)
    for i in range(20):
        try:
            os.remove(p)
            return
        except FileNotFoundError:
            return
        except OSError:
            time.sleep(0.05 * (i + 1))


def _pid_alive(pid):
    if os.name == "nt":
        import ctypes
        h = ctypes.windll.kernel32.OpenProcess(0x1000, False, int(pid))   # PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION
        if not h:
            return False
        code = ctypes.c_ulong()
        ctypes.windll.kernel32.GetExitCodeProcess(h, ctypes.byref(code))
        ctypes.windll.kernel32.CloseHandle(h)
        return code.value == 259                                          # STILL_ACTIVE
    try:
        os.kill(int(pid), 0)
        return True
    except (OSError, ValueError):
        return False


def outstanding_indeterminate():
    """In-flight markers whose outcome is unknown: marked INDETERMINATE, or left by a process that is gone."""
    out = []
    if not EVIDENCE_LOG:
        return out
    try:
        names = sorted(os.listdir(_inflight_dir()))
    except OSError:
        return out
    for n in names:
        if not n.endswith(".json"):
            continue
        try:
            with open(os.path.join(_inflight_dir(), n), encoding="utf-8") as fh:
                rec = json.load(fh)
        except (OSError, ValueError):
            rec = {"cid": n[:-5], "status": "UNREADABLE marker"}
        if rec.get("cid") in _ACTIVE:
            continue
        if rec.get("status") == "INDETERMINATE" or rec.get("status") == "UNREADABLE marker" \
                or (rec.get("os") in (None, os.name) and not _pid_alive(rec.get("pid") or 0)):
            out.append(rec)
    return out


def reconcile_resolve(cid, verdict, note):
    """Record what a reconcile found (applied / not-applied / partial) and clear the marker. Touches no game."""
    _evidence({"ev": "reconciled", "cid": cid, "as": verdict, "note": note, "t": _ev_now(), "pid": os.getpid()},
              required=True)
    _inflight_clear(cid)


def _args_sha(params):
    return hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(params or {}, sort_keys=True, default=str).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:16]


def _player_log_candidates():
    """Every place Player.log might be, best first."""
    yield DEFAULT_PLAYER_LOG
    if WSL:
        import glob
        for base in sorted(glob.glob("/mnt/c/Users/*/AppData/LocalLow/"
                                     "Ludeon Studios/RimWorld by Ludeon Studios")):
            yield os.path.join(base, "Player.log")

GABP_VERSION = "gabp/1"
BRIDGE_VERSION = "1.0"

# Anything not on this list is assumed to mutate the game until proven otherwise.
READ_ONLY_PREFIXES = ("list_", "get_", "search_", "find_", "compile_", "ping")
# Reads the prefixes cannot see. companion_handshake only reports the companion's profile; treated as mutating it was
# refused whenever any earlier call had an UNKNOWN outcome (testq: 4 jobs INVALID/HARNESS 10-27..10-29), so the
# harness could not even read the state it needed to reconcile.
# running_mods only lists LoadedModManager's running mods (and hashes an assembly file when asked); without this entry
# live_def_check's owner lookup was refused on every call (exit 3) and every unresolved def read UNMEASURED (2026-11-02).
READ_ONLY_TOOLS = ("jawa/companion_handshake", "jawa/running_mods")
# jawa/static_call runs ANY static method, so it is mutating by default. These (type, method) pairs are reviewed getters:
# a caller that declares its call read-only (CLI --read-only-static, live_def_check._bridge(read_only_static=True)) passes
# the guard for these and only these. TIDAL_LOCK_FIX_PRESET_NAME_WAS_MISSING's readback was refused as not read-only on
# every relentless live run (RELENTLESS_LIVE_FIX_GAME_UP_NOTHING_MEASURED). Add a pair only after reading its source.
READ_ONLY_STATIC_CALLS = frozenset((
    ("AlienWorlds.PlanetTypeManager", "get_Current"),             # a property getter
    ("HarmonyLib.Harmony", "HasAnyPatches"),                      # Harmony's own query: a dictionary read
    ("Worldbuilder.World_ExposeData_Patch", "get_WorldPresetName"),   # a static property getter
    ("RimMandrake.Biomes.RM_WorldDecals", "Info"),                # builds a string from statics
    ("RimMandrake.Biomes.RM_WorldDecals", "Probe"),               # ContentFinder lookup, no cache, no build
))


def read_only_static(params):
    """-> None when this jawa/static_call is a reviewed read (READ_ONLY_STATIC_CALLS), else why it is not."""
    p = params if isinstance(params, dict) else {}
    pair = (p.get("type"), p.get("method"))
    return None if pair in READ_ONLY_STATIC_CALLS else "%s.%s is not a reviewed read-only static call" % pair

# Tools the owner has RETIRED. The bridge still registers them; we refuse to be the
# thing that calls one. A doc saying "don't" is read by whoever already looked it up;
# this is read by whoever didn't.
RETIRED_TOOLS = {
    "jawa/hot_reload_defs": (
        "RETIRED by the owner on 2026-09-03 as unstable.\n"
        "  Measured on the 589-mod list: it hung the bridge ~5 minutes, then left the\n"
        "  game unable to generate ANY pawn - jawa/spawn_pawn NRE'd on Muffalo, Hare,\n"
        "  Colonist, Tribesperson and Villager alike, and vanilla's own debug spawn\n"
        "  named it: \"The given key 'RimWorld.HairDef' was not present in the\n"
        "  dictionary\". Every health flag read green throughout.\n"
        "  DO INSTEAD: deploy the XML and restart on the 19-mod minimal list - 22\n"
        "  seconds - then read the field back with jawa/get_defs.\n"
        "  Ruling: skills/rimworld-modding/SKILL.md #2.\n"
        "  Evidence: infrastructure/state/items/closed/HOT_RELOAD_DEFS_BREAKS_PAWNGEN_1.md\n"
        "  To run the sanctioned re-test (MINIMAL LIST ONLY, where a broken game costs\n"
        "  22 s): set RIMBRIDGE_ALLOW_RETIRED=jawa/hot_reload_defs in the environment."
    ),
}


def _retired(tool):
    """The refusal text for a retired tool, or None. Honours the explicit override."""
    why = RETIRED_TOOLS.get(tool)
    if why is None:
        return None
    allowed = os.environ.get("RIMBRIDGE_ALLOW_RETIRED", "")
    if tool in [t.strip() for t in allowed.split(",") if t.strip()]:
        return None
    return why


class RimBridgeError(RuntimeError):
    """A GABP-level failure: bad handshake, transport break, or tool error."""


class RetiredToolError(RimBridgeError):
    """The tool exists on the bridge and the owner has retired it. See RETIRED_TOOLS."""


# MODCHECK_DRIVERS_HARDEN_OWN_TIMEOUT_MIDCALL: a process that will be hard-killed at a known time (modcheck drivers.py
# sets this to the epoch second of its subprocess timeout) gets no NEW mutating call that could still be in flight
# then: a kill mid call strands an UNKNOWN-outcome marker that refuses every later mutation of the run.
DEADLINE_ENV = "RIMBRIDGE_CALL_DEADLINE"


class DeadlineError(RimBridgeError):
    """A mutating call refused before it started: it might not finish before RIMBRIDGE_CALL_DEADLINE."""


def _deadline_left():
    """Seconds until RIMBRIDGE_CALL_DEADLINE: None only when UNSET. A set value that is unparseable or NaN reads as
    already expired (-inf): the process may still be killed at a time it cannot read, so a mutation fails closed
    (RIMBRIDGE_DEADLINE_FIX_NAN_FAILS_OPEN -- 'nan' compared False and let every mutation run). 'inf' is no limit."""
    raw = os.environ.get(DEADLINE_ENV)
    if raw is None:
        return None
    try:
        at = float(raw)
    except ValueError:
        return float("-inf")
    if at != at:   # NaN
        return float("-inf")
    return at - time.time()


class DriverHeldError(RimBridgeError):
    """A mutating call on this machine's game while another live process holds the driver lock."""


CROSS_ENV = "RM_BRIDGE_CROSS_WHY"       # a deliberate crossing: the reason, recorded on the call's evidence row
_LOOPBACK = ("127.0.0.1", "localhost", "::1")


def _driver_crossing(host):
    """The holder's refusal text if a mutation here would cross him, else None. Only this machine's game: the lock
    file is this machine's. The guard lives next door in rimflow; a client copied without it says so and goes on."""
    if host not in _LOOPBACK:
        return None
    try:
        rimflow_dir = str(_rm_pl.Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "rimflow")
        if rimflow_dir not in sys.path:
            sys.path.append(rimflow_dir)
        import host_guard
        return host_guard.crossing()
    except Exception as ex:
        print("[rimbridge_client] driver lock not checked: %s" % ex, file=sys.stderr)
        return None


class UnknownParameterError(RimBridgeError):
    """A tool was called with an argument key its schema does not declare.

    BRIDGE_DROPS_UNKNOWN_PARAMS_1, proven live 2026-08-26: the bridge DISCARDS a
    key it does not know, silently, and runs the tool on its defaults.

        jawa/new_allowed_area {label: "CHECK_correct"}           -> label "CHECK_correct"
        jawa/new_allowed_area {name:  "CHECK_wrong", banana: 42} -> label "Area 3"   success:true
        jawa/time_clock       {zzz: "nonsense"}                  -> full correct payload

    ⛔ The server is not ours and cannot be changed. This is the CLIENT-side guard,
    and it turns each of those into a loud local failure before a byte is sent.
    """


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# token discovery
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

_PORT_RE = re.compile(r"\[RimBridge\].*?on port\s+(\d+)")
_TOKEN_RE = re.compile(r"\[RimBridge\]\s*Bridge token:\s*([0-9A-Za-z._\-]+)")


def discover_from_log(path=None):
    """Scrape the NEWEST '[RimBridge] ... on port N' / 'Bridge token: X' pair.

    Returns (host, port, token); port/token are None if the log has no bridge
    lines. Last match wins on purpose - Player.log is append-only across
    restarts, so the first match is usually a dead session from hours ago.
    """
    paths = [path] if path else list(_player_log_candidates())
    port = token = None
    for candidate in paths:
        port = token = None
        try:
            with open(candidate, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as fh:
                for line in fh:
                    if "[RimBridge]" not in line:
                        continue
                    m = _PORT_RE.search(line)
                    if m:
                        port = int(m.group(1))
                    m = _TOKEN_RE.search(line)
                    if m:
                        token = m.group(1)
        except OSError:
            continue
        if token:
            break
    if token is None and port is None:
        return DEFAULT_HOST, None, None
    return DEFAULT_HOST, port, token


def resolve_endpoint(host=None, port=None, token=None, log_path=None):
    """CLI arg > env > Player.log > module default, per field independently."""
    log_host = log_port = log_token = None
    if host is None or port is None or token is None:
        log_host, log_port, log_token = discover_from_log(log_path)

    host = host or os.environ.get("RIMBRIDGE_HOST") or log_host or DEFAULT_HOST
    if port is None:
        env_port = os.environ.get("GABP_SERVER_PORT")
        port = int(env_port) if env_port else (log_port or DEFAULT_PORT)
    token = token or os.environ.get("GABP_TOKEN") or log_token or DEFAULT_TOKEN
    return host, int(port), token


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# the bridge
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

class RimBridge:
    """One GABP session over one TCP socket.

    Not thread-safe and not meant to be: the bridge serialises onto RimWorld's
    main thread anyway, so a second concurrent caller buys nothing but
    interleaved frames.
    """

    def __init__(self, host=DEFAULT_HOST, port=DEFAULT_PORT, token="",
                 timeout=30.0, connect_timeout=5.0, client_name="rimbridge_client.py"):
        self.host = host
        self.port = int(port)
        self.token = token or ""
        self.timeout = timeout
        self.connect_timeout = connect_timeout
        self.client_name = client_name
        self.sock = None
        self.buf = b""
        # tool name -> set of declared argument keys. Populated lazily on the first
        # guarded call; None until then, and a tool absent from it is UNCHECKED,
        # never "has no parameters". See _declared_params.
        self._param_index = None
        self.welcome = None
        self.events = []          # unsolicited event envelopes seen while reading
        self._session_started = None
        self._session_calls = 0

    # -- lifecycle ---------------------------------------------------------

    def connect(self):
        """Open the socket and complete session/hello. Raises on refusal."""
        try:
            self.sock = socket.create_connection((self.host, self.port),
                                                 timeout=self.connect_timeout)
        except OSError as ex:
            # Under WSL this is never "the game is down" -- RimBridge binds
            # Windows loopback and WSL2 is NAT-mode, so there is no route at
            # all. Saying "is RimWorld running?" here sends the reader to check
            # a game that is running fine. Name the real cause instead.
            if WSL:
                raise RimBridgeError(
                    "cannot reach the bridge from WSL, and no amount of "
                    "retrying will fix it.\n"
                    "  RimBridge binds Windows loopback; WSL2 is NAT-mode, so "
                    "%s:%s has no route from here.\n"
                    "  This says NOTHING about whether RimWorld is running.\n"
                    "  Re-run under Windows Python:  python.exe %s"
                    % (self.host, self.port,
                       " ".join(sys.argv) or "<your script>")) from ex
            raise RimBridgeError(
                "cannot reach the bridge at %s:%s (%s) - is RimWorld running "
                "with RimBridgeServer enabled?" % (self.host, self.port, ex)) from ex
        self.sock.settimeout(self.timeout)
        self.welcome = self._hello()
        self._session_started = time.time()
        self._session_calls = 0
        return self

    def close(self):
        if self._session_started is not None:
            _log_session(self._session_started, self._session_calls, self.client_name)
            self._session_started = None
        if self.sock is not None:
            try:
                self.sock.shutdown(socket.SHUT_RDWR)
            except OSError:
                pass
            try:
                self.sock.close()
            except OSError:
                pass
            self.sock = None

    def __enter__(self):
        if self.sock is None:
            self.connect()
        return self

    def __exit__(self, *exc):
        self.close()
        return False

    # -- framing -----------------------------------------------------------

    def _send(self, envelope):
        body = json.dumps(envelope, separators=(",", ":")).encode("utf-8")
        head = ("Content-Length: %d\r\nContent-Type: application/json\r\n\r\n"
                % len(body)).encode("ascii")
        self.sock.sendall(head + body)

    def _recv_raw(self):
        """Read exactly one framed JSON message. Tolerates LF-only headers."""
        while b"\r\n\r\n" not in self.buf and b"\n\n" not in self.buf:
            self._fill()
        sep = b"\r\n\r\n" if b"\r\n\r\n" in self.buf else b"\n\n"
        head, _, rest = self.buf.partition(sep)
        length = None
        for line in head.decode("ascii", "replace").splitlines():
            if line.lower().startswith("content-length:"):
                length = int(line.split(":", 1)[1].strip())
        if length is None:
            raise RimBridgeError("framed message had no Content-Length header: %r"
                                 % head[:200])
        self.buf = rest
        while len(self.buf) < length:
            self._fill()
        body, self.buf = self.buf[:length], self.buf[length:]
        return json.loads(body.decode("utf-8"))

    def _fill(self):
        try:
            chunk = self.sock.recv(65536)
        except socket.timeout as ex:
            raise RimBridgeError(
                "timed out after %ss waiting for the bridge; RimWorld may be in a "
                "long event or the call may be frame-bound" % self.timeout) from ex
        if not chunk:
            raise RimBridgeError("bridge closed the connection")
        self.buf += chunk

    def _recv_response(self, want_id):
        """Read until the response with our id arrives; park events aside."""
        while True:
            msg = self._recv_raw()
            if msg.get("type") == "event":
                self.events.append(msg)
                continue
            if msg.get("id") == want_id or want_id is None:
                return msg
            if msg.get("id") in getattr(self, "abandoned", ()):
                # The late answer to a request this client already gave up on (timed out). MEASURED live 2026-10-01:
                # FlowWorks' heavy flood ticks outran the call timeout, and the late reply then made every LATER call
                # in the run die with "unexpected response id". It belongs to nobody; drop it.
                self.abandoned.discard(msg.get("id"))
                continue
            # A response for some other id means the stream desynced.
            raise RimBridgeError("unexpected response id %r (wanted %r)"
                                 % (msg.get("id"), want_id))

    def _request(self, method, params=None):
        rid = str(uuid.uuid4())
        self._send({
            "v": GABP_VERSION,
            "id": rid,
            "type": "request",
            "method": method,
            "params": params or {},
        })
        try:
            msg = self._recv_response(rid)
        except RimBridgeError as ex:
            if str(ex).startswith("timed out"):
                if not hasattr(self, "abandoned"):
                    self.abandoned = set()
                self.abandoned.add(rid)
            raise
        err = msg.get("error")
        if err:
            raise RimBridgeError("%s failed: %s" % (
                method, err.get("message") if isinstance(err, dict) else err))
        return msg.get("result")

    # -- handshake ---------------------------------------------------------

    def _hello(self):
        params = {
            "token": self.token,
            "bridgeVersion": BRIDGE_VERSION,
            "platform": sys.platform,
            "clientInfo": {
                "name": self.client_name,
                "version": "1.0.0",
                "author": "rimworld-project",
            },
        }
        try:
            return self._request("session/hello", params)
        except RimBridgeError as ex:
            if "Invalid session/hello parameters" not in str(ex):
                raise
            # Fall back to the minimum the server documents as required.
            return self._request("session/hello", {"token": self.token})

    # -- public API --------------------------------------------------------

    def list_tools(self):
        """tools/list -> the live tool descriptors. Never mutates."""
        result = self._request("tools/list") or {}
        return result.get("tools", [])

    # --- the unknown-parameter guard --------------------------------------
    #
    # The descriptor key holding a tool's schema is not something this client can
    # know offline, and guessing one and finding nothing would make the guard pass
    # everything - the exact failure it exists to prevent. So it tries the
    # candidates in order and, when none of them yields keys, says UNCHECKED out
    # loud rather than returning a clean answer.
    _SCHEMA_KEYS = ("inputSchema", "input_schema", "parameters", "schema", "arguments")

    @staticmethod
    def _declared_params(descriptor):
        """The argument keys a tool descriptor declares, or None if UNMEASURABLE.

        ⛔ Returns None - NOT an empty set - when no schema can be found. An empty
        set would read as "this tool takes no arguments" and reject every correct
        call; None means "this client could not look", and the caller warns.
        """
        if not isinstance(descriptor, dict):
            return None
        for key in RimBridge._SCHEMA_KEYS:
            node = descriptor.get(key)
            if isinstance(node, dict):
                props = node.get("properties")
                if isinstance(props, dict):
                    # An EMPTY dict is a real, common shape (51/432 live tools,
                    # rimworld/get_game_info among them) meaning "declares zero
                    # params" - not "no schema found". The old `and props` here
                    # made every such tool read UNCHECKED, silently disabling the
                    # unknown-parameter guard on exactly the tools where a typo'd
                    # key is most likely: one that takes no real arguments at all.
                    return set(props.keys())
                if node and "properties" not in node and all(isinstance(k, str) for k in node):
                    # a bare {name: spec} map rather than a JSON-Schema object
                    return set(node.keys())
        return None

    def _param_map(self):
        if self._param_index is None:
            index = {}
            for d in self.list_tools():
                name = d.get("name") if isinstance(d, dict) else None
                if name:
                    index[name] = self._declared_params(d)
            self._param_index = index
        return self._param_index

    def check_params(self, tool, params):
        """Raise UnknownParameterError for any key the tool does not declare.

        Returns a one-line reason string when the check could NOT be made, and None
        when it passed. A caller that ignores the return value still gets the raise.
        """
        if not params:
            return None
        try:
            declared = self._param_map().get(tool, "missing")
        except Exception as exc:                      # a tools/list failure must not
            return "UNCHECKED: tools/list failed (%s)" % exc   # break the call itself
        if declared == "missing":
            return "UNCHECKED: %s is not in tools/list" % tool
        if declared is None:
            return "UNCHECKED: no readable schema on %s" % tool
        unknown = sorted(k for k in params if k not in declared)
        if unknown:
            raise UnknownParameterError(
                "%s does not declare %s. The bridge would DISCARD %s silently and run "
                "on its defaults, returning success. Declared: %s"
                % (tool, ", ".join(unknown),
                   "them" if len(unknown) > 1 else "it",
                   ", ".join(sorted(declared)) or "(none)"))
        return None

    def call(self, tool, params=None, check=True):
        """tools/call. NOTHING here stops you calling a destructive tool.

        🔑 It DOES stop you calling one with a misspelled argument: `check` runs the
        unknown-parameter guard first (BRIDGE_DROPS_UNKNOWN_PARAMS_1). Pass
        check=False only when you mean to send a key the schema does not declare.
        """
        why = _retired(tool)
        if why is not None:
            raise RetiredToolError("%s is RETIRED - refusing to call it.\n  %s" % (tool, why))
        if check:
            unchecked = self.check_params(tool, params)
            if unchecked:
                print("[rimbridge_client] %s -> %s" % (tool, unchecked), file=sys.stderr)
        mutating = not self.looks_read_only(tool, params)
        crossed = None
        if mutating:
            crossed = _driver_crossing(self.host)
            if crossed and not os.environ.get(CROSS_ENV):
                raise DriverHeldError("refusing %s: %s. Wait for `rimflow bridge who` to read free, or take the bridge; "
                                      "to cross him on purpose set %s=<why>" % (tool, crossed, CROSS_ENV))
            left = _deadline_left()
            if left is not None and left < self.timeout + self.connect_timeout:
                raise DeadlineError("refusing %s: %.0f s to %s (=%r), less than this call's %.0f s timeout + %.0f s "
                                    "connect: a kill mid call would strand an UNKNOWN-outcome marker"
                                    % (tool, max(left, 0), DEADLINE_ENV, os.environ.get(DEADLINE_ENV),
                                       self.timeout, self.connect_timeout))
            pending = outstanding_indeterminate()
            if pending:
                raise IndeterminateError(
                    "refusing %s: %d earlier mutating call(s) have an UNKNOWN outcome (%s). A retry could apply it "
                    "twice. Read the game with read-only calls, then record the answer:\n  python "
                    "rimbridge_client.py --reconcile [--resolve CID --as applied|not-applied|partial --note \"...\"]"
                    % (tool, len(pending), ", ".join("%s %s" % (p.get("cid"), p.get("tool")) for p in pending[:3])))
        cid = uuid.uuid4().hex[:16]
        start = {"ev": "start", "cid": cid, "run": _RUN_ID, "t": _ev_now(), "tool": tool,
                 "args_sha256": _args_sha(params), "mutating": mutating, "pid": os.getpid(), "os": os.name,
                 "seat": os.environ.get("RIMFLOW_SEAT") or os.environ.get("AGENT_SEAT"),
                 "script": os.path.basename(sys.argv[0]) if sys.argv else "", "client": self.client_name,
                 "endpoint": "%s:%s" % (self.host, self.port)}
        if crossed:
            start["crossed_holder"] = "%s: %s" % (os.environ[CROSS_ENV], crossed)
        try:
            _evidence(start, required=mutating)
            if mutating:
                _inflight_write(dict(start, status="in-flight"))
        except OSError as ex:
            raise RimBridgeError("refusing mutating call %s: its evidence (intent) could not be recorded at %s "
                                 "(%s)" % (tool, EVIDENCE_LOG, ex))
        _ACTIVE.add(cid)
        t0 = time.time()
        self._session_calls += 1
        try:
            out = self._request("tools/call", {"name": tool, "arguments": params or {}})
        except RimBridgeError as ex:
            answered = " failed: " in str(ex)          # the server replied with an error: outcome known
            status = "error" if answered else ("INDETERMINATE" if mutating else "lost")
            timed_out = "timed out" in str(ex).lower()
            # outcome/transport/timeout folded in from the retired rimdrive.obs_events (design 08 P5)
            outcome = "error" if answered else ("timeout" if timed_out else "lost")
            _evidence({"ev": "end", "cid": cid, "status": status, "ms": int((time.time() - t0) * 1000),
                       "error": str(ex)[:300], "t": _ev_now(), "outcome": outcome, "timeout": timed_out,
                       "transport": "ok" if answered else outcome})
            if mutating and status == "INDETERMINATE":
                try:
                    _inflight_write(dict(start, status="INDETERMINATE", error=str(ex)[:300]))
                except OSError:
                    pass
            else:
                _inflight_clear(cid)
            _ACTIVE.discard(cid)
            raise
        except BaseException as ex:
            _ACTIVE.discard(cid)                      # KeyboardInterrupt etc: marker stays, read as orphaned
            # Name the exception: a bare "client interrupted" left testq J20261026T182927Z-c2508c's set_fog death
            # (an OSError/ValueError escaping the socket read <1 s after the send, game alive) undiagnosable.
            why = "client interrupted: %s: %s" % (type(ex).__name__, str(ex)[:240])
            try:
                _evidence({"ev": "end", "cid": cid, "status": "INDETERMINATE" if mutating else "lost",
                           "ms": int((time.time() - t0) * 1000), "error": why, "t": _ev_now(),
                           "outcome": "lost", "timeout": False, "transport": type(ex).__name__})
            except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - evidence is best effort here; the original exception must propagate
                pass
            if mutating:
                try:
                    _inflight_write(dict(start, status="INDETERMINATE", error=why))
                except OSError:
                    pass
            raise
        ok_success = out.get("success") if isinstance(out, dict) else None
        _evidence({"ev": "end", "cid": cid, "status": "ok", "ms": int((time.time() - t0) * 1000), "t": _ev_now(),
                   "success": ok_success, "outcome": "reply_fail" if ok_success is False else "ok",
                   "timeout": False, "transport": "ok"})
        _inflight_clear(cid)
        _ACTIVE.discard(cid)
        return out

    def looks_read_only(self, tool, params=None):
        """Cheap heuristic only - a False here is a warning, a True is not a promise. A jawa/static_call is a read only
        when this client was told so (static_reads, the --read-only-static declaration) AND it is a reviewed pair."""
        leaf = tool.split("/", 1)[-1]
        if tool == "jawa/static_call" and getattr(self, "static_reads", False):
            return read_only_static(params) is None
        return leaf.startswith(READ_ONLY_PREFIXES) or tool in READ_ONLY_TOOLS


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CLI
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def _main(argv=None):
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        description="Query a live RimWorld through the RimBridgeServer GABP bridge.")
    ap.add_argument("--host")
    ap.add_argument("--port", type=int)
    ap.add_argument("--token")
    ap.add_argument("--log", dest="log_path", help="Player.log to scrape for port/token")
    ap.add_argument("--timeout", type=float, default=30.0)
    ap.add_argument("--list-tools", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--call", metavar="TOOL")
    ap.add_argument("--json", dest="params", default="{}",
                    help="JSON object of tool arguments")
    ap.add_argument("--raw", action="store_true", help="dump the full envelope result")
    ap.add_argument("--yes-i-know-this-is-live", action="store_true",
                    help="required to call a tool that fails the read-only heuristic")
    ap.add_argument("--read-only-static", action="store_true",
                    help="declare a jawa/static_call a read; accepted only for READ_ONLY_STATIC_CALLS")
    ap.add_argument("--reconcile", action="store_true",
                    help="list mutating calls with an UNKNOWN outcome (touches no game); with --resolve, record one")
    ap.add_argument("--resolve", metavar="CID")
    ap.add_argument("--as", dest="verdict", choices=("applied", "not-applied", "partial"))
    ap.add_argument("--note", default="")
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)

    if args.reconcile:
        if args.resolve:
            if not args.verdict or not args.note:
                print("--resolve needs --as and a --note saying what you read to decide", file=sys.stderr)
                return 2
            reconcile_resolve(args.resolve, args.verdict, args.note)
            print("reconciled %s as %s" % (args.resolve, args.verdict))
            return 0
        pend = outstanding_indeterminate()
        print("evidence log %s; %d mutating call(s) with UNKNOWN outcome" % (EVIDENCE_LOG, len(pend)))
        for p in pend:
            print("  %s  %s  %s  args %s  pid %s %s  %s" % (p.get("cid"), p.get("t"), p.get("tool"),
                                                         p.get("args_sha256"), p.get("pid"), p.get("script"),
                                                         p.get("error", p.get("status"))))
        return 1 if pend else 0

    host, port, token = resolve_endpoint(args.host, args.port, args.token, args.log_path)
    if not token:
        print("no bridge token found (CLI, env GABP_TOKEN, or Player.log)", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2

    if args.call and not args.list_tools:
        probe = RimBridge(host, port, token, timeout=args.timeout)
        try:
            params = json.loads(args.params)
        except ValueError:
            params = None
        if args.read_only_static:
            why = "--read-only-static is for jawa/static_call" if args.call != "jawa/static_call" else read_only_static(params)
            if why:
                print("REFUSING '%s': %s" % (args.call, why), file=sys.stderr)
                return 3
            probe.static_reads = True
        if not probe.looks_read_only(args.call, params) and not args.yes_i_know_this_is_live:
            print("REFUSING '%s': it does not look read-only. This drives a LIVE game.\n"
                  "Pass --yes-i-know-this-is-live if you really mean it." % args.call,
                  file=sys.stderr)
            return 3

    try:
        with RimBridge(host, port, token, timeout=args.timeout) as rb:
            if args.list_tools:
                tools = rb.list_tools()
                print(json.dumps({"count": len(tools), "tools": tools}, indent=2))
            if args.call:
                rb.static_reads = bool(args.read_only_static)
                out = rb.call(args.call, json.loads(args.params))
                print(json.dumps(out, indent=2))
            if not args.list_tools and not args.call:
                print(json.dumps({"welcome": rb.welcome}, indent=2))
    except RimBridgeError as ex:
        print("bridge error: %s" % ex, file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(_main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""selftest_peaceful_landing.py -- GRAVSHIP_PEACEFUL_SETTLEMENT_LANDING_1 (offline half).

Owner, 2026-10-02: "We need a way for gravship to land properly in settlement and not be seen as attacking."

A buyer-pit site (the Hutt slave pit first) is a trading post. Vanilla 1.6 decides "attack or visit" from data on the
site's SitePartDefs, in four places (read from the decompiled 1.6 Assembly-CSharp; anchors below):

  GravshipUtility.ArriveNewMap            attack iff parent is Settlement, or a Site whose parts ALL say
                                          considerEnteringAsAttack, and the parent's faction is someone else's
  CaravanArrivalAction_VisitSite.DoEnter  AffectRelationsOnAttacked iff ANY part says considerEnteringAsAttack
  TransportersArrivalAction_VisitSite     attack iff faction is someone else's and the MAIN part says it
  Site.PostMapGenerate                    detection-raid countdown unless a part disallowsAutomaticDetectionTimerStart
                                          or the map was spawned by a gravship landing
  Site.GravShipCanLandOn                  MainSitePartDef.gravShipsCanLandOn and no map yet

This test ports those predicates, evaluates them on every SitePartDef that carries RM_BuyerPitSiteExtension, checks the
quest node only ever hands such a site to a faction that is not hostile, and plants breaks that must go red. When the
decompile is on disk its source lines are matched against the ported expressions, so a game update that changes them
fails here instead of passing on a stale port.

Not covered (prior art, GravTide Docs/vanilla-traps.md): a full faction SETTLEMENT has no peaceful path in vanilla --
ArriveNewMap always attacks one, and a loaded settlement map with no hostile on it is destroyed by
SettlementDefeatUtility.CheckDefeated. The Hutt test site is a Site, so neither applies.

    python3 src/RimMandrake/KeelHoist/selftest_peaceful_landing.py
    python3 src/RimMandrake/KeelHoist/selftest_peaceful_landing.py --live   # A1: the RUNNING game loaded the fields;
                                       one read-only jawa/get_defs; exit 0 holds, 1 the game says otherwise, 2 UNMEASURED
"""
import copy
import glob
import os
import re
import sys
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
SRC = os.path.normpath(os.path.join(HERE, "..", ".."))
PIT_CS = os.path.join(HERE, "Source", "RM_PitBuyer.cs")
EXT = "RimMandrake.KeelHoist.RM_BuyerPitSiteExtension"
DECOMP = os.environ.get("RM_DECOMP_1_6", "/mnt/d/ClaudeWork/rimmandrake/SOORRAK_LOOP/full")
ANCHORS = [   # (file under the decompile, text that must appear verbatim) -- the expressions ported below
    ("RimWorld/GravshipUtility.cs", "(orGenerateMap.Parent is Settlement || (orGenerateMap.Parent is Site site2 && "
     "site2.parts.All((SitePart part) => part.def.considerEnteringAsAttack))) && orGenerateMap.Parent.Faction != null "
     "&& orGenerateMap.Parent.Faction != Faction.OfPlayer"),
    ("RimWorld.Planet/CaravanArrivalAction_VisitSite.cs",
     "if (site.parts.Any((SitePart part) => part.def.considerEnteringAsAttack))"),
    ("RimWorld.Planet/TransportersArrivalAction_VisitSite.cs",
     "if (site.Faction != null && site.Faction != Faction.OfPlayer && site.MainSitePartDef.considerEnteringAsAttack)"),
    ("RimWorld.Planet/Site.cs", "if (!parts.Any((SitePart p) => p.def.disallowsAutomaticDetectionTimerStart) && "
     "!map.wasSpawnedViaGravShipLanding)"),
    ("RimWorld.Planet/Site.cs", "if (MainSitePartDef.gravShipsCanLandOn)"),
    ("RimWorld/SitePartDef.cs", "public bool considerEnteringAsAttack = true;"),
    ("RimWorld/SitePartDef.cs", "public bool disallowsAutomaticDetectionTimerStart;"),
    ("RimWorld/SitePartDef.cs", "public bool gravShipsCanLandOn;"),
]
DEFAULTS = {"considerEnteringAsAttack": True, "disallowsAutomaticDetectionTimerStart": False, "gravShipsCanLandOn": False}
FAILS = []


def check(name, cond, detail=""):
    print("%s  %s %s" % ("ok  " if cond else "FAIL", name, "" if cond else detail))
    if not cond:
        FAILS.append(name)


def _bool(node, field):
    el = node.find(field)
    if el is None or el.text is None:
        return DEFAULTS[field]
    t = el.text.strip().lower()
    if t not in ("true", "false"):
        raise ValueError("%s/%s is not a bool: %r" % (node.findtext("defName"), field, el.text))
    return t == "true"


def part_fields(node):
    return {f: _bool(node, f) for f in DEFAULTS}


def buyer_pit_parts():
    """-> {defName: (path, SitePartDef element)} for every SitePartDef in src/ carrying the buyer-pit extension."""
    out = {}
    for path in glob.glob(os.path.join(SRC, "**", "*.xml"), recursive=True):
        try:
            root = ET.parse(path).getroot()
        except ET.ParseError:
            continue
        for d in root.iter("SitePartDef"):
            if any(li.get("Class") == EXT for li in d.iter("li")):
                out[d.findtext("defName")] = (path, d)
    return out


# ---- vanilla 1.6 predicates, ported (parts = list of field dicts; parts[0] is the main part) ----
def gravship_entry_is_attack(parts, parent_is_settlement, faction, player="player"):
    hit = parent_is_settlement or all(p["considerEnteringAsAttack"] for p in parts)
    return hit and faction is not None and faction != player


def caravan_entry_is_attack(parts):
    return any(p["considerEnteringAsAttack"] for p in parts)


def transporters_entry_is_attack(parts, faction, player="player"):
    return faction is not None and faction != player and parts[0]["considerEnteringAsAttack"]


def detection_countdown_starts(parts, via_gravship_landing):
    return not any(p["disallowsAutomaticDetectionTimerStart"] for p in parts) and not via_gravship_landing


def gravship_can_land(parts, has_map=False):
    return parts[0]["gravShipsCanLandOn"] and not has_map


def peaceful_findings(parts):
    """Every way the site would be treated as hostile on entry; [] is a trading post."""
    f = []
    if not gravship_can_land(parts):
        f.append("gravship cannot land")
    if gravship_entry_is_attack(parts, False, "keepers"):
        f.append("gravship landing is an attack")
    if caravan_entry_is_attack(parts):
        f.append("caravan entry is an attack")
    if transporters_entry_is_attack(parts, "keepers"):
        f.append("transport pods are an attack")
    for via in (True, False):
        if detection_countdown_starts(parts, via):
            f.append("detection raid countdown starts (%s)" % ("gravship" if via else "caravan"))
    return f


def faction_findings(cs):
    """The quest node must hand the site only to a faction that is not hostile to the player."""
    m = re.search(r"private static Faction FactionFor\(SitePartDef def\)\s*\{(.*?)\n        \}", cs, re.S)
    if not m:
        return ["FactionFor not found"]
    body, f = m.group(1), []
    if "!f.HostileTo(Faction.OfPlayer)" not in body:
        f.append("FactionFor may pick a hostile faction")
    if "SiteMaker.MakeSite(def, tile, faction)" not in cs:
        f.append("site is not made with FactionFor's faction")
    return f


def live(timeout=60):
    """A1: the running game's RUT_HuttSlavePit carries the shipped values (a MayRequire-gated def can silently not load)."""
    sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(SRC, "RimMandrake", "Utils"))
    import live_def_check as L
    want = {"considerEnteringAsAttack": False, "disallowsAutomaticDetectionTimerStart": True, "gravShipsCanLandOn": True}
    reply, why = L._bridge("jawa/get_defs", {"defs": "SitePartDef/RUT_HuttSlavePit", "fields": ",".join(want)}, timeout)
    if reply is None:
        print("UNMEASURED: " + why)
        return 2
    recs = [d for d in (reply.get("defs") or []) if isinstance(d, dict)] if isinstance(reply, dict) else []
    if len(recs) != 1 or not isinstance(recs[0].get("found"), bool):
        print("UNMEASURED: not one get_defs record: %r" % (reply,))
        return 2
    d = recs[0]
    if d["found"] is not True:
        running = L.call_running_mods(timeout)
        if running is None or "mandrake.rm.keelhoist" not in running:
            print("UNMEASURED: RUT_HuttSlavePit not loaded and mandrake.rm.keelhoist is not in the running load (%s)"
                  % ("unread" if running is None else "%d mods" % len(running)))
            return 2
        print("FAIL: mandrake.rm.keelhoist is running but SitePartDef/RUT_HuttSlavePit did not resolve")
        return 1
    if not isinstance(d.get("fields"), dict):
        print("UNMEASURED: record has no fields map: %r" % (d,))
        return 2
    got = {k: str(d["fields"].get(k)).strip().lower() for k in want}
    bad = {k: got[k] for k, v in want.items() if got[k] != str(v).lower()}
    print(("FAIL: " if bad else "PASS: ") + "RUT_HuttSlavePit live fields %r" % got)
    return 1 if bad else 0


def main():
    # anchors: the port is only as good as its match to the game's code
    if os.path.isdir(DECOMP):
        for rel, text in ANCHORS:
            p = os.path.join(DECOMP, rel)
            body = open(p, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read() if os.path.exists(p) else ""
            check("decompile anchor %s: %s" % (rel, text[:48]), text in body, "not found in " + p)
    else:
        print("note  decompile not on disk (%s): anchors UNMEASURED, ported predicates trusted as committed" % DECOMP)

    # the predicates themselves, on vanilla defaults (a SitePartDef that says nothing is a raid target)
    dflt = [dict(DEFAULTS)]
    check("sanity: a default site part is an attack every way and gets a raid countdown by caravan",
          gravship_entry_is_attack(dflt, False, "x") and caravan_entry_is_attack(dflt)
          and transporters_entry_is_attack(dflt, "x") and detection_countdown_starts(dflt, False))
    check("sanity: a Settlement is an attack even when every part says no",
          gravship_entry_is_attack([dict(DEFAULTS, considerEnteringAsAttack=False)], True, "x"))
    check("sanity: own or factionless site is never an attack by gravship",
          not gravship_entry_is_attack(dflt, False, "player") and not gravship_entry_is_attack(dflt, False, None))

    parts = buyer_pit_parts()
    check("sanity: RUT_HuttSlavePit is found among buyer-pit site parts", "RUT_HuttSlavePit" in parts, sorted(parts))
    for name, (path, node) in sorted(parts.items()):
        fl = peaceful_findings([part_fields(node)])
        check("%s (%s): landing, caravan and pods are visits, no detection raid" % (name, os.path.relpath(path, SRC)),
              fl == [], fl)
        # planted breaks, on a copy (never the shipped file)
        for field, bad, must in (("considerEnteringAsAttack", "true", "gravship landing is an attack"),
                                 ("disallowsAutomaticDetectionTimerStart", "false", "detection raid countdown starts (caravan)"),
                                 ("gravShipsCanLandOn", "false", "gravship cannot land")):
            n2 = copy.deepcopy(node)
            el = n2.find(field)
            if el is None:
                el = ET.SubElement(n2, field)
            el.text = bad
            got = peaceful_findings([part_fields(n2)])
            check("break %s: %s=%s -> %s" % (name, field, bad, must), must in got, got)
        n3 = copy.deepcopy(node)
        n3.remove(n3.find("considerEnteringAsAttack"))
        check("break %s: considerEnteringAsAttack removed (vanilla default true) -> attack" % name,
              "gravship landing is an attack" in peaceful_findings([part_fields(n3)]))
        # a second, default part on the same site: gravship needs ALL to say attack, caravan needs ANY
        two = [part_fields(node), dict(DEFAULTS)]
        check("%s + a default part: gravship stays a visit, caravan turns attack (vanilla All vs Any)" % name,
              not gravship_entry_is_attack(two, False, "keepers") and caravan_entry_is_attack(two))

    cs = open(PIT_CS, encoding="utf-8").read()
    check("quest node gives the site only a non-hostile faction", faction_findings(cs) == [], faction_findings(cs))
    check("break: FactionFor drops the hostility filter -> red",
          "FactionFor may pick a hostile faction" in faction_findings(cs.replace(" && !f.HostileTo(Faction.OfPlayer)", "")))

    print("\n%s: %d failure(s)" % ("FAIL" if FAILS else "PASS", len(FAILS)))
    return 1 if FAILS else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(live() if "--live" in sys.argv[1:] else main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""live_log_check.py -- does the RUNNING game's Player.log name a token in an error line? Read-only, no bridge call.

    python3 src/RimMandrake/Utils/live_log_check.py --absent RUT_ExplosiveGrowthRoster --absent RUT_PaleMoss [--warnings]

For criteria worded "Player.log carries no error naming X" (RA_S09_LIVE_WIRE_ONE_REAL_LEAF). A line is an error line when
it matches ERROR_RE (with --warnings, WARN_RE too); a token is matched as a literal substring of such a line.

--never TOKEN fails on ANY line naming the token, error word or not. Player.log carries no level marker: a Log.Warning
is bare text (stack traces are off), so a warning without the word "warn" in it is invisible to --warnings. Name such a
message by its own text with --never ("[RM Minerals] quarry", "name only disabled mineables").

Exit 0 no error line names any token, 1 one does (a real FAIL; the lines are printed), 2 UNMEASURED: no running game,
a log older than the running game (it belongs to an earlier session), or a log without the anchor (default
"Bridge token:", printed once the load finished and RimBridge came up: a log before that has not seen the load's
errors yet). Pair it with live_def_check.py when the criterion also needs the mod to be loaded: an absent token in a
load that never had the mod is not a pass, and this file cannot tell.
"""
import argparse
import datetime
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
PASS, FAIL, UNMEASURED = 0, 1, 2
# Word-ended so an identifier is not an error: RUT_ErrorPlant and "0 errors" are not error lines, NullReferenceException,
# "2 errors" and "Config error in" are. The tokens and every underscore identifier are blanked out first (MASK_RE).
ERROR_RE = re.compile(r"errors?\b|exceptions?\b|\bfailed\b|\bcould not\b|\bcouldn't\b", re.I)
WARN_RE = re.compile(r"warn(ing)?s?\b", re.I)
NONE_RE = re.compile(r"\b(0|no|zero|without)\s+(errors?|exceptions?|warnings?)\b", re.I)
IDENT_RE = re.compile(r"\w*_\w*")
# A line that continues the record above it (a stack trace, an inner exception, a [Ref] stub), not a message of its
# own. Blank lines never split a record: "Exception:\n\n  defName: X" is one record. A failed patch prints its file on
# the next line, unindented ("file: C:\\...\\Patches\\X.xml"): without `file: ` a token naming the patch file was missed.
CONT_RE = re.compile(r"^(\s|at |file: |\(Filename|--- |Rethrow|\[0x|\[Ref |(Verse|RimWorld|UnityEngine|System|HarmonyLib|Mono)\.\S*[:(])")
ANCHOR = "Bridge token:"


def records(text):
    """-> [(first line number, [lines])]: a message line plus the continuation lines under it."""
    out = []
    for n, line in enumerate(text.splitlines(), 1):
        if not line.strip():
            continue
        if out and CONT_RE.match(line):
            out[-1][1].append(line)
        else:
            out.append((n, [line]))
    return out


def judge(text, tokens, warnings=False, anchor=ANCHOR, never=()):
    """-> (exit code, lines). Pure: `text` is the whole Player.log. A record (a message and its stack trace) fails when
    any of its lines is an error line (with `warnings`, a warning line too) and any of its lines names a token, as a
    literal substring: RUT_PaleMoss also hits RUT_PaleMossLarge, a false FAIL at worst, never a false PASS."""
    if anchor and anchor not in text:
        return UNMEASURED, ["UNMEASURED: the log has no %r yet: the load has not finished" % anchor]
    hits, recs = [], records(text)
    for n, lines in recs:
        named = [t for t in never if any(t in x for x in lines)]
        if named:
            hits.append("FAIL line %d names %s, which may never appear: %s" % (n, ", ".join(named),
                                                                              " | ".join(x.strip() for x in lines)[:240]))
    mask = re.compile("|".join(re.escape(t) for t in sorted(tokens, key=len, reverse=True)))

    def bad(line):
        line = NONE_RE.sub(" ", IDENT_RE.sub(" ", mask.sub(" ", line)))
        return ERROR_RE.search(line) or (warnings and WARN_RE.search(line))

    for n, lines in recs if tokens else ():
        named = [t for t in tokens if any(t in x for x in lines)]
        if named and any(bad(x) for x in lines):
            hits.append("FAIL line %d names %s: %s" % (n, ", ".join(named), " | ".join(x.strip() for x in lines)[:240]))
    if hits:
        return FAIL, hits[:40] + (["... %d more" % (len(hits) - 40)] if len(hits) > 40 else [])
    return PASS, (["PASS no %s line names %s" % ("error or warning" if warnings else "error", ", ".join(tokens))] if tokens
                  else []) + (["PASS no line names %s" % ", ".join(never)] if never else [])


def game_started():
    """The running RimWorld's start, epoch seconds to the millisecond; None when none or two run, or it cannot be read."""
    try:
        r = subprocess.run(["powershell.exe", "-NoProfile", "-Command",
                            "Get-Process RimWorldWin64 -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | ForEach-Object "
                            "{ $_.StartTime.ToUniversalTime().ToString('yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.fffZ') }"],
                           capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=60, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL)
        lines = [x.strip() for x in r.stdout.splitlines() if x.strip()]
        if len(lines) != 1:
            return None
        return datetime.datetime.strptime(lines[0], "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%fZ").replace(
            tzinfo=datetime.timezone.utc).timestamp()
    except (OSError, ValueError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired):
        return None


def main(argv=None):
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument("--absent", action="append", default=[], metavar="TOKEN")
    ap.add_argument("--never", action="append", default=[], metavar="TOKEN",
                    help="any line naming this fails, error word or not (a Log.Warning has no marker in Player.log)")
    ap.add_argument("--warnings", action="store_true", help="a warning line naming a token fails too")
    ap.add_argument("--log", default=None, help="another log (default: game_paths.PLAYER_LOG); skips the game check")
    a = ap.parse_args(argv)
    tokens = [t for t in (x.strip() for x in a.absent) if t]
    never = [t for t in (x.strip() for x in a.never) if t]
    if not tokens and not never:
        print("UNMEASURED: no token to look for")
        return UNMEASURED
    path = a.log
    if path is None:
        sys.path.insert(0, HERE)
        from game_paths import PLAYER_LOG as path
        started = game_started()
        if started is None:
            print("UNMEASURED: no running game")
            return UNMEASURED
        try:
            if os.path.getmtime(path) <= started:
                print("UNMEASURED: %s was last written before the running game started" % path)
                return UNMEASURED
        except OSError as e:
            print("UNMEASURED: %s" % e)
            return UNMEASURED
    try:
        with open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as f:
            text = f.read()
    except OSError as e:
        print("UNMEASURED: %s" % e)
        return UNMEASURED
    if a.log is None and game_started() != started:
        print("UNMEASURED: the running game changed while the log was read")
        return UNMEASURED
    code, lines = judge(text, tokens, a.warnings, never=never)
    print("\n".join(lines))
    print({PASS: "VERDICT PASS", FAIL: "VERDICT FAIL", UNMEASURED: "VERDICT UNMEASURED"}[code])
    return code


def safe_main(argv=None):
    """main(), where nothing may escape: an uncaught exception exits 1, which the runner would record as a FAIL."""
    try:
        return main(argv)
    except SystemExit:
        raise
    except BaseException as e:
        sys.stdout.write("UNMEASURED: " + ascii("%s: %s" % (type(e).__name__, str(e)[:200])) + "\n")
        return UNMEASURED


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(safe_main())

scripts.src/RimMandrake/HugeThings/northstar/tit:
"""titan_test_races_live.py -- the five titan rows that needed a body-size 8/20 creature (TITANIC_BODYSIZE_TEST_RACE_1, criterion A2),
driven with the harness-only test races of src/RimMandrake/HugeThingsTestRaces on whatever Playing map is current.

  python3 src/RimMandrake/HugeThings/northstar/titan_test_races_live.py [--site X,Z] [--out FILE]

LIST: Huge Things (mandrake.rm.hugethings) + Huge Things Test Races (mandrake.rm.hugethingstestraces), all five DLC; nothing else.
The probes are the static hooks in Source/Titanic/Events/TitanValidationHooks.cs, called through jawa/static_call. The map is
DIRTIED (a T3 and a T2 are killed into corpses): use a throwaway quicktest map. Settings touched are snapshotted and restored.

Rows {id, criterion, status PASS|FAIL|UNMEASURED, cls MOD|SITE|HARNESS, detail}; JSON -> Transient/modcheck/ by default.
  R1 t2_t3_tiers                    TierReport: T2 race reads T2, T3 reads T3, the forced-out control None, Elephant T1;
                                    tiered races carry CompTitanicWake.
  R2 t3_corpse_becomes_a_harvest_site KillTitanAt T3 -> one more RM_TitanicCorpseSite; KillTitanAt T2 -> none more.
  R3 butcher_yield_curve_reduces_t1_t2_yield ButcherYieldReport: T2 meat = control meat x the kernel factor (< 1), within
                                    per-pawn rounding; the same-mass forced-out control is unreduced.
  R4 t2_holes_thin_roofs_and_crushes_walls RoofWallProbe: a T2 stepping into a roofed wall cell holes RoofConstructed and damages
                                    or breaks the wood wall; the control leaves both.
  R5 thick_roof_route_excluded      ThickRoofCostProbe: a T2's step cost under RoofRockThick >= 2000 and above open ground;
                                    the control's two costs are equal.
Refuses to judge (UNMEASURED SITE) when the custom tier ladder (tierThresholdsCustom, startup-read) is on.
Exit 0 when all five rows are PASS or a FAIL classified MOD (the criterion: each row gets a verdict); 1 otherwise.
"""
import argparse
import json
import os
import re
import sys
import time

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
REPO = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(HERE, "..", "..", "..", ".."))
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(REPO, "src", "RimMandrake", "Utils"))

ITEM = "TITANIC_BODYSIZE_TEST_RACE_1"
HOOKS = "RimMandrake.TitanicCreatures.TitanValidationHooks"
SETTINGS = "RimMandrake.HugeThings.RM_HugeThingsSettings"
T2, T3, CTL = "RM_TestTitanT2", "RM_TestTitanT3", "RM_TestTitanT2Control"
FIELDS = {"giantAnimalsEnabled": True, "wakeEnabled": True, "wakeRoofHolingEnabled": True, "yieldCurveEnabled": True,
          "roofAvoidanceEnabled": True, "corpseSiteEnabled": True}
THICK_ROOF_PENALTY = 2000.0          # Patch_ThickRoofAvoidance.ThickRoofPenalty
ROWS = ("t2_t3_tiers", "t3_corpse_becomes_a_harvest_site", "butcher_yield_curve_reduces_t1_t2_yield",
        "t2_holes_thin_roofs_and_crushes_walls", "thick_roof_route_excluded")


def kv(txt, key):
    m = re.search(r"\b%s=(\S+)" % re.escape(key), txt or "")
    return m.group(1) if m else None


def parse_tiers(txt):
    """TierReport text -> {kind: {tier, adultTier, bodySize, wakeComp}}."""
    out = {}
    for part in (txt or "").split(" | "):
        name = part.split(" ", 1)[0]
        out[name] = {k: kv(part, k) for k in ("tier", "adultTier", "bodySize", "wakeComp")}
    return out


def sites(txt):
    m = re.match(r"sites=(\d+)", txt or "")
    return int(m.group(1)) if m else None


class Run(object):
    def __init__(self, rb, out):
        self.rb, self.out, self.rows, self.log = rb, out, [], []

    def call(self, tool, **kw):
        try:
            r = self.rb.call(tool, kw) or {}
        except Exception as ex:  # noqa: BLE001
            r = {"success": False, "error": "call raised: %s" % ex}
        self.log.append((tool, kw, str(r)[:400]))
        return r

    def hook(self, method, args=""):
        r = self.call("jawa/static_call", type=HOOKS, method=method, args=args)
        txt = str(r.get("result") if r.get("result") is not None else r.get("error") or r.get("message") or r)
        print("    %s(%s) -> %s" % (method, args, txt[:400]), flush=True)
        return r.get("success") is True and not txt.startswith("FAIL"), txt

    def get(self, f):
        return self.call("jawa/mod_settings_field", typeName=SETTINGS, action="get", field=f).get("value")

    def put(self, f, v):
        # restore-check: ok -- main() snapshots FIELDS first and puts every one back in its finally
        return self.call("jawa/mod_settings_field", typeName=SETTINGS, action="set", field=f, value=str(v)).get("success")

    def ticks(self, n):
        done = 0
        while done < n:
            k = min(1000, n - done)
            self.call("rimworld/step_game_ticks", ticks=k)
            done += k

    def row(self, rid, status, cls, detail):
        self.rows.append(dict(id=rid, item=ITEM, criterion="A2", status=status, cls=cls, detail=detail))
        print("  %-42s %-10s %-7s %s" % (rid, status, cls, detail[:300]), flush=True)
        self.save()

    def save(self):
        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(self.out), exist_ok=True)
        with open(self.out, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            json.dump(dict(script="titan_test_races_live.py", item=ITEM, when=time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S"), rows=self.rows,
                           calls=self.log), f, indent=1, default=str)


def verdict(rows):
    """0 when every one of ROWS has exactly a PASS or a MOD-classified FAIL; 1 otherwise (UNMEASURED, HARNESS, missing)."""
    got = {r["id"]: r for r in rows}
    for rid in ROWS:
        r = got.get(rid)
        if r is None or not (r["status"] == "PASS" or (r["status"] == "FAIL" and r["cls"] == "MOD")):
            return 1
    return 0


def judge_tiers(rep):
    want = {T2: "T2", T3: "T3", CTL: "None", "Elephant": "T1"}
    bad = [k for k, v in want.items() if rep.get(k, {}).get("tier") != v or rep.get(k, {}).get("adultTier") != v]
    bad += ["%s wakeComp" % k for k in (T2, T3) if rep.get(k, {}).get("wakeComp") != "True"]
    return bad


def judge_yield(t2, ctl):
    """(status, detail) from two ButcherYieldReport lines. Each of n pawns rounds its meat once (GenMath.RoundRandom), so the
    T2 total sits within n of control x factor."""
    try:
        n = int(kv(t2, "n"))
        m2, mc, f = int(kv(t2, "meat")), int(kv(ctl, "meat")), float(kv(t2, "factor"))
        fc = float(kv(ctl, "factor"))
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return None, "unparsable: %s || %s" % (t2, ctl)
    d = "T2 meat=%d control meat=%d factor=%.4f (control factor %.4f) expected %.1f +- %d" % (m2, mc, f, fc, mc * f, n)
    if kv(ctl, "tier") != "None" or fc != 1.0:
        return "FAIL", "control is tiered or curved: " + d
    if mc <= 0:
        return None, "control butchered no meat: " + d
    ok = f < 1.0 and m2 < mc and abs(m2 - mc * f) <= n
    return ("PASS" if ok else "FAIL"), d


def judge_roof(t2, ctl):
    try:
        hb, ha = int(kv(t2, "wallHpBefore")), int(kv(t2, "wallHpAfter"))
        cb, ca = int(kv(ctl, "wallHpBefore")), int(kv(ctl, "wallHpAfter"))
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return None, "unparsable: %s || %s" % (t2, ctl)
    holed = kv(t2, "roofAfter") == "none"
    crushed = kv(t2, "wallDestroyed") == "True" or ha < hb
    ctl_clean = kv(ctl, "roofAfter") == "RoofConstructed" and kv(ctl, "wallDestroyed") == "False" and ca == cb
    d = "T2 roofAfter=%s wall %d->%d; control roofAfter=%s wall %d->%d" % (kv(t2, "roofAfter"), hb, ha, kv(ctl, "roofAfter"), cb, ca)
    return ("PASS" if holed and crushed and ctl_clean else "FAIL"), d


def judge_thick(t2, ctl):
    try:
        o2, k2 = float(kv(t2, "costOpen")), float(kv(t2, "costThick"))
        oc, kc = float(kv(ctl, "costOpen")), float(kv(ctl, "costThick"))
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return None, "unparsable: %s || %s" % (t2, ctl)
    ok = k2 >= THICK_ROOF_PENALTY and k2 > o2 and kc == oc
    return ("PASS" if ok else "FAIL"), "T2 open=%.1f thick=%.1f; control open=%.1f thick=%.1f" % (o2, k2, oc, kc)


def body(R, cells):
    ok, txt = R.hook("TierReport", "%s,%s,%s,Elephant" % (T2, T3, CTL))
    rep = parse_tiers(txt) if ok else {}
    if not ok or any(k not in rep or rep[k].get("tier") is None for k in (T2, T3, CTL)):
        R.row("t2_t3_tiers", "UNMEASURED", "HARNESS", "test races not readable (is mandrake.rm.hugethingstestraces on the list?): "
              + txt[:200])
        return
    bad = judge_tiers(rep)
    R.row("t2_t3_tiers", "FAIL" if bad else "PASS", "MOD", ("wrong: %s; " % bad if bad else "") + txt[:300])

    # R4 / R5 first: they need clean open cells, and R2 leaves corpses and sites behind.
    def probe(method, kind):
        for (x, z) in cells:
            ok, t = R.hook(method, "%s|%d,%d" % (kind, x, z))
            if ok:
                return t
            if "not usable" not in t:
                return None
        return None

    rw2, rwc = probe("RoofWallProbe", T2), probe("RoofWallProbe", CTL)
    st, d = judge_roof(rw2, rwc) if rw2 and rwc else (None, "no usable cell or probe failed: %s || %s" % (rw2, rwc))
    R.row("t2_holes_thin_roofs_and_crushes_walls", st or "UNMEASURED", "MOD" if st else "SITE", d)

    tr2, trc = probe("ThickRoofCostProbe", T2), probe("ThickRoofCostProbe", CTL)
    st, d = judge_thick(tr2, trc) if tr2 and trc else (None, "no usable cell or probe failed: %s || %s" % (tr2, trc))
    R.row("thick_roof_route_excluded", st or "UNMEASURED", "MOD" if st else "SITE", d)

    ok2, y2 = R.hook("ButcherYieldReport", T2)
    okc, yc = R.hook("ButcherYieldReport", CTL)
    st, d = judge_yield(y2, yc) if ok2 and okc else (None, "hook failed: %s || %s" % (y2, yc))
    R.row("butcher_yield_curve_reduces_t1_t2_yield", st or "UNMEASURED", "MOD" if st else "HARNESS", d)

    ok, before = R.hook("SiteReport")
    n0 = sites(before) if ok else None
    (x, z), (x2, z2) = cells[0], cells[1]
    ok3, k3 = R.hook("KillTitanAt", "%s|%d,%d" % (T3, x, z))
    R.ticks(300)
    _, mid = R.hook("SiteReport")
    ok2, k2 = R.hook("KillTitanAt", "%s|%d,%d" % (T2, x2, z2))
    R.ticks(300)
    _, after = R.hook("SiteReport")
    n1, n2 = sites(mid), sites(after)
    if n0 is None or n1 is None or n2 is None or not ok3 or not ok2:
        R.row("t3_corpse_becomes_a_harvest_site", "UNMEASURED", "HARNESS", "sites %r/%r/%r kills %s || %s" % (n0, n1, n2, k3, k2))
        return
    good = "tier=T3" in k3 and "tier=T2" in k2 and n1 == n0 + 1 and n2 == n1
    R.row("t3_corpse_becomes_a_harvest_site", "PASS" if good else "FAIL", "MOD",
          "sites before=%d after T3 kill=%d after T2 kill=%d; %s; %s" % (n0, n1, n2, k3[:120], k2[:120]))


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--site", default="", help="first probe cell X,Z (default: map centre, then offsets)")
    ap.add_argument("--out", default=os.path.join(REPO, "Transient", "modcheck",
                                                  "titan_test_races_%s.json" % time.strftime("%Y%m%dT%H%M%S")))
    a = ap.parse_args()
    from rimbridge_client import RimBridge, discover_from_log
    host, port, token = discover_from_log()
    with RimBridge(host, port, token, timeout=180.0) as rb:
        R = Run(rb, a.out)
        snap = dict((f, R.get(f)) for f in FIELDS)
        if any(v is None for v in snap.values()):
            R.row("settings_snapshot", "UNMEASURED", "HARNESS", "could not read %r" % snap)
            print("rows -> %s" % a.out)
            return 1
        mi = R.call("jawa/map_info")
        size = mi.get("size") or mi.get("mapSize") or {}
        try:
            cx, cz = int(size.get("x")) // 2, int(size.get("z")) // 2
        except (TypeError, ValueError, AttributeError):
            cx = cz = 125
        if a.site:
            cx, cz = [int(v) for v in a.site.split(",")]
        cells = [(cx + dx, cz + dz) for dx, dz in ((0, 0), (12, 0), (-12, 0), (0, 12), (0, -12), (12, 12), (-12, -12), (20, 20))]
        try:
            unset = [f for f, v in FIELDS.items() if not R.put(f, v) or str(R.get(f)).lower() != str(v).lower()]
            custom = R.get("tierThresholdsCustom")
            if str(custom).lower() != "false":
                # a startup-read setting: the expected tiers are the default 4/8/20 ladder, so a custom one cannot be judged here
                R.row("settings_ladder", "UNMEASURED", "SITE", "tierThresholdsCustom=%r: the ladder is not the default 4/8/20" % custom)
            elif unset:
                R.row("settings_set", "UNMEASURED", "HARNESS", "could not set %r: no row can be judged" % unset)
            else:
                body(R, cells)
        finally:
            lost = [f for f, v in snap.items() if not R.put(f, v) or str(R.get(f)).lower() != str(v).lower()]
            if lost:
                print("RESTORE FAILED for %r (wanted %r)" % (lost, dict((f, snap[f]) for f in lost)), flush=True)
            R.save()
    print("rows -> %s" % a.out)
    v = verdict(R.rows)
    print("VERDICT: %s (%d rows)" % ("PASS" if v == 0 else "FAIL", len(R.rows)))
    return v


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
