#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""modcheck -- the scripted mod-functionality validator (pre-playtest).

    python.exe src/RimMandrake/Utils/modcheck/cli.py run <mod> [<mod>...] [--debug]
    python3     src/RimMandrake/Utils/modcheck/cli.py status
    python3     src/RimMandrake/Utils/modcheck/cli.py declare <mod> minor --why "..."
    python3     src/RimMandrake/Utils/modcheck/cli.py rename-key <old> <new> --why "..."
    python3     src/RimMandrake/Utils/modcheck/cli.py forget-key <key> --why "..."
    python3     src/RimMandrake/Utils/modcheck/cli.py validate <mod> [--owner-said "..."]
    python3     src/RimMandrake/Utils/modcheck/cli.py validate <mod> --delegated --judge-verdict <json>
    python3     src/RimMandrake/Utils/modcheck/cli.py review <mod> --owner-said "..."
    python3     src/RimMandrake/Utils/modcheck/cli.py record <mod> --result <json> [--tier T]

`record` (2026-10-02) records a functional script's LIVE result (e.g.
FlowWorks/northstar/validation_v2.py) through status.record_run WITHOUT
touching ModsConfig.xml -- it refuses a stale result (mod hash moved), a run
whose live mod set is not the declared tier, and an aborted run (record.py).

`run` drives a live bridge session and needs `python.exe` (Windows) for the
same WSL-loopback reason every other bridge driver does
(rimbridge_client.py). `status` and `declare` touch only
`infrastructure/state/modcheck_status.json` and run fine under plain
`python3`.

`rename-key` and `forget-key` are the two verbs `modcheck_status.json` owed
the naming migration (MEASURED 2026-09-17: `FluidCanals` sat GREEN under its
dead pre-rename name while the mod ships as `FlowWorks`) -- the only
sanctioned way to move or drop a key, since hand-editing that file is
forbidden.

`validate` and `review` are the two OWNER-AUTHORISED verbs added 2026-09-15
(design/RimMandrake/north_star_validation_spec.md): `validate` turns a mod's
agent-drafted `## north star` checklist into a binding bar, `review` records
that he has read a run's sheet with his own eyes -- required once, before a
mod's first GREEN. Both take his verbatim `--owner-said` and neither re-derives
his judgement; `validate` with no `--owner-said` prints the bar and writes
nothing, so the lines can be read to him first. `validate --delegated
--judge-verdict <json>` binds NEW bars without his words (owner 2026-10-26,
delegation_policy.md §2.1) and refuses any loosening against the section's last
validated version in git history; the walk's `validated-by:` then names the
class and the judge's verdict file.
"""
import argparse
import os
import sys

_HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
if _HERE not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, _HERE)
_UTILS = os.path.dirname(_HERE)
if _UTILS not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, _UTILS)


def main(argv=None):
    argv = sys.argv[1:] if argv is None else list(argv)
    if argv[:1] == ["metrics"]:     # its own argparse (metrics.py --help); listed below for discoverability
        import metrics
        return metrics.main(argv[1:])
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__,
                                 formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    sub = ap.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)

    p_run = sub.add_parser("run")
    p_run.add_argument("mods", nargs="+",
                       help="mod folder name(s), e.g. Pits")
    p_run.add_argument("--item", action="append", default=[],
                       help="ITEM_ID: TARGETED run of the chains that item maps to (its rows cite it, or its "
                            "ledger text names a chain/row), recorded against it; refused if nothing maps. "
                            "MOD=ITEM_ID: only the ledger item a run is recorded against (default "
                            "MODCHECK_<MOD>_RUN_1)")
    p_run.add_argument("--chains", default="",
                       help="TARGETED: comma-separated chain names to run (one mod)")
    p_run.add_argument("--rows", default="",
                       help="TARGETED: comma-separated row ids; each row's chain runs as a PREFIX and stops after its "
                            "last requested row, the tail recorded NOT_RUN (one mod)")
    p_run.add_argument("--preview", action="store_true",
                       help="TARGETED: print the per-chain plan (requested -> prerequisites -> executed -> skipped) "
                            "and stop: no mod-list swap, no game")
    p_run.add_argument("--full", action="store_true",
                       help="the whole suite: a scheduled sweep, at most daily (owner 2026-10-25). A run with no "
                            "--chains/--rows/--item ITEM_ID is refused without it")
    # focused_testing_plan option B (all opt-in; without them a run behaves exactly as before)
    p_run.add_argument("--reuse", choices=("off", "report", "on"), default=None,
                       help="external-driver rows with no result at the current mod hash: 'report' (the default when "
                            "unset) tags a result whose runtime+test manifest and DLL still match as reusable@<file> "
                            "and leaves the row UNMEASURED; 'on' takes its status as reused@<file> (never fresh_green); "
                            "'off' does not look (sets MODCHECK_REUSE, modcheck/reuse.py)")
    p_run.add_argument("--drivers", choices=("on", "off"), default=None,
                       help="'on': before the chains, run the suite's external live drivers (suite.live_drivers, e.g. "
                            "FlowWorks northstar/thirst_live.py) whose chains are selected, so their rows are measured at "
                            "this mod hash; the SteveDesktop worker passes it (sets MODCHECK_RUN_DRIVERS, modcheck/drivers.py)")
    p_run.add_argument("--purpose", choices=("fix", "guard", "sweep", "sensitivity", "flake", "commission"),
                       default=None,
                       help="why this run happens (plan 2026-10-25 section 3): fix/guard let the known-good gate skip a "
                            "chain whose recorded PASS still holds; sweep/sensitivity/flake/commission run everything "
                            "and only report would_skip. Default: sweep with --full, guard otherwise "
                            "(sets MODCHECK_PURPOSE, modcheck/gate.py)")
    p_run.add_argument("--gate", choices=("on", "shadow", "off"), default=None,
                       help="the known-good gate: 'on' (default) skips per --purpose, 'shadow' never skips but "
                            "records would_skip, 'off' computes nothing (sets MODCHECK_GATE)")
    p_run.add_argument("--canary", action="store_true",
                       help="run the vanilla canary (Steel spawn/read-back/destroy, a live colonist, Playing) before "
                            "the first chain; red -> every chain records one UNMEASURED HARNESS row, no body runs")
    p_run.add_argument("--validity", action="store_true",
                       help="arm the validity checks (menu drop, colonist count 0, hostile arrival): a FAIL they "
                            "explain becomes UNMEASURED/invalid with the FAIL kept as a lead, no finding")
    p_run.add_argument("--changed", default=None, metavar="RANGE|WORKTREE",
                       help="print the chains a change (git range plus uncommitted files; WORKTREE = uncommitted "
                            "only) SUGGESTS, and stop: nothing runs from a suggestion (one mod)")
    p_run.add_argument("--seat", default=None,
                       help="ledger seat for the run's verify/findings when RIMFLOW_SEAT/AGENT_SEAT do not reach "
                            "this process (Windows python.exe); with none the run is still recorded, ledger skipped")
    p_run.add_argument("--debug", action="store_true")
    p_run.add_argument("--situational", action="store_true",
                       help="wrap every chain in the situational envelope: bland map, python-enforced "
                            "tick budget, detector sweeps, evidence+screenshot on any surprise")
    p_run.add_argument("--policy", choices=["abort", "record"], default="abort",
                       help="what a surprise does: abort the component (UNMEASURED) or just record it")
    p_run.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true",
                       help="exercise the orchestration with no game, no "
                            "subprocess side effects (selftest-shaped)")

    p_status = sub.add_parser("status")
    p_status.add_argument("mod", nargs="?")

    p_decl = sub.add_parser("declare")
    p_decl.add_argument("mod")
    p_decl.add_argument("severity", choices=["minor"])
    p_decl.add_argument("--why", required=True)

    p_ren = sub.add_parser("rename-key", help="move a registry entry from an old "
                                              "mod key to its new name")
    p_ren.add_argument("old")
    p_ren.add_argument("new")
    p_ren.add_argument("--why", required=True)

    p_forget = sub.add_parser("forget-key", help="delete a registry entry outright "
                                                 "-- for an orphaned key with no "
                                                 "successor worth preserving")
    p_forget.add_argument("key")
    p_forget.add_argument("--why", required=True)

    p_val = sub.add_parser("validate", help="record the owner's validation of a "
                                            "mod's `## north star` checklist")
    p_val.add_argument("mod")
    p_val.add_argument("--owner-said",
                       help="his verbatim words. Required to WRITE; omit to "
                            "print the lines that would bind and change nothing")
    p_val.add_argument("--by-card", help="a decision he took by question card: "
                       "'<question -> option>'. Stands in for --owner-said")
    p_val.add_argument("--per-ruling", help="with --why: a Conductor instruction "
                       "(conductor_authority.RULING). Stands in for --owner-said")
    p_val.add_argument("--why", help="the Conductor's text; alone it grants nothing")
    p_val.add_argument("--delegated", action="store_true",
                       help="bind NEW bars without his words (owner 2026-10-26, "
                            "delegation_policy.md §2.1): refused if the section "
                            "loosens its last validated version; needs --judge-verdict")
    p_val.add_argument("--judge-verdict",
                       help="with --delegated: the judge's verdict JSON under "
                            "infrastructure/state/delegated/ (top-level verdict PASS)")

    p_rev = sub.add_parser("review", help="record that the owner reviewed a "
                                          "mod's sheet -- once, before its first GREEN")
    p_rev.add_argument("mod")
    p_rev.add_argument("--owner-said")
    p_rev.add_argument("--per-ruling", help="with --why: a Conductor instruction "
                       "(conductor_authority.RULING). Stands in for --owner-said")
    p_rev.add_argument("--why", help="the Conductor's text; alone it grants nothing")
    p_rev.add_argument("--run-id", help="defaults to the mod's last recorded run")

    p_rec = sub.add_parser("record", help="record a functional script's live result "
                                          "(no ModsConfig swap) -- refuses stale/off-tier runs")
    p_rec.add_argument("mod")
    p_rec.add_argument("--result", required=True, help="the script's result JSON")
    p_rec.add_argument("--tier", default=None,
                       help="modset_builder tier the run must have been on "
                            "(default: the mod name lowercased)")
    p_rec.add_argument("--extensions", default=None,
                       help="step 4's result JSON (northstar/extension_proof.py --live), for a mod that "
                            "ships one; omitted, step 4 records UNMEASURED and the checkout cannot be green")

    p_lint = sub.add_parser("lint", help="every identifier a validation walk "
                                         "names must exist (walklint)")
    p_lint.add_argument("--warn", action="store_true",
                        help="also print WARN findings (UNKNOWN_ID, BAD_FILE), "
                             "which never affect the exit code")

    p_floor = sub.add_parser("floor", help="the visual/settings floor triage "
                                           "-- read-only, no bridge, no "
                                           "ModsConfig.xml write")
    p_floor.add_argument("--all", action="store_true", required=True,
                         help="every mod with a validation walk, one row "
                              "each (the only mode today)")

    sub.add_parser("doctor", help="the five registries keyed on a mod's folder "
                                  "name must agree with disk. Reports and "
                                  "stops -- never repairs; the ownership calls "
                                  "it surfaces are the owner's")

    sub.add_parser("metrics", add_help=False,
                   help="the daily test-orchestration metrics file (WASTE, unclassified share, lanes, gate misses, "
                        "alarms) at <testq>/metrics/<day>.json; `metrics --help` for its flags (modcheck/metrics.py)")

    args = ap.parse_args(argv)

    if args.cmd == "record":
        import record
        code, msg, _ = record.record(args.mod, args.result, args.tier or args.mod.lower(),
                                    ext_path=args.extensions)
        print(msg)
        return code

    if args.cmd == "doctor":
        import doctor
        return doctor.main([])

    if args.cmd == "lint":
        import runner
        import walklint
        findings, counts = walklint.lint(runner.ROOT)
        print("walklint: %d walks, %d packageIds, %d symbols indexed"
              % (counts["walks"], counts["packageids"], counts["symbols"]))
        if not counts["walks"] or not counts["packageids"]:
            print("UNMEASURED: an index came back empty -- this is a query bug, "
                  "not a clean repo. Refusing to report zero findings.")
            return 2
        shown = [f for f in findings
                 if f[0] == walklint.FAIL or args.warn]
        for f in shown:
            print(walklint.format_finding(f))
        n_fail = sum(1 for f in findings if f[0] == walklint.FAIL)
        n_warn = sum(1 for f in findings if f[0] == walklint.WARN)
        print("%d FAIL, %d WARN%s"
              % (n_fail, n_warn, "" if args.warn else "  (--warn to see WARNs)"))

        import readline_registry
        try:
            rl_findings, rl_counts = readline_registry.lint(runner.ROOT)
        except FileNotFoundError as exc:
            print("UNMEASURED: %s" % exc)
            return 2
        print("readline_registry: %d walks, %d registry ids, %d `shared` "
              "citations checked" % (rl_counts["walks"], rl_counts["registry_ids"],
                                     rl_counts["citations"]))
        for f in rl_findings:
            print(readline_registry.format_finding(f))
        print("%d FAIL" % len(rl_findings))

        return 1 if (n_fail or rl_findings) else 0

    if args.cmd == "floor":
        import floor
        import runner
        rows, footer = floor.triage(runner.ROOT)
        if not rows:
            print("UNMEASURED: no validation walks found -- this is a query "
                  "bug, not a clean repo. Refusing to report zero rows.")
            return 2
        print(floor.format_triage(rows, footer))
        return 0

    if args.cmd == "status":
        import status
        data = status.load()
        if args.mod:
            print(status.check(args.mod, _mod_dir_or_die(args.mod)))
            return 0
        if not data:
            print("no mods recorded")
            return 0
        import northstar
        import runner
        # Re-derive per row rather than printing entry["status"]. The stored
        # field is what made this summary disagree with `status <mod>`: it
        # printed `Pits GREEN` while the per-mod view printed STALE, and
        # `FluidCanals GREEN` for a mod renamed away weeks earlier.
        for mod, entry in sorted(data.items()):
            walk = northstar.find_walk(runner.ROOT, mod)
            ns = northstar.parse(walk) if walk else None
            bar = ("checklist %s (%d lines)" % (ns["state"], len(ns["must_show"]))
                   if ns and ns["present"] else "no checklist")
            live = status.check_or_orphaned(mod)
            stored = entry.get("status")
            drift = "" if live.split(" (")[0] == stored else "   [stored: %s]" % stored
            run = ""
            if entry.get("source"):     # a `modcheck record` entry: say what it was run at
                try:
                    cur = status.mod_hash(runner.find_mod_dir(mod))
                    at = "current hash" if cur == entry.get("hash") else "STALE hash"
                except RuntimeError:
                    at = "no mod folder"
                cnt = (entry.get("components") or {}).get("counts") or {}
                try:
                    s4 = status.step4_live(entry, runner.find_mod_dir(mod))
                except RuntimeError:
                    s4 = None
                run = "   [run %s at %s %s; %s%s]" % (
                    entry["source"].get("result", "?").rsplit("/", 1)[-1], at,
                    (entry.get("hash") or "")[:12],
                    " ".join("%s %d" % kv for kv in sorted(cnt.items())),
                    "" if s4 is None else "; step 4 %s" % s4)
            if len(live) > 60:
                live = live[:57] + "..."
            print("%-30s %-22s %s%s%s" % (mod, live, bar, drift, run))
        return 0

    if args.cmd == "declare":
        import status
        entry = status.declare_minor(args.mod, _mod_dir_or_die(args.mod), args.why)
        print("declared minor: %s at %s" % (args.mod, entry["hash"][:12]))
        return 0

    if args.cmd == "rename-key":
        import status
        status.rename_key(args.old, args.new, args.why)
        print("renamed: %s -> %s" % (args.old, args.new))
        return 0

    if args.cmd == "forget-key":
        import status
        status.forget_key(args.key, args.why)
        print("forgotten: %s" % args.key)
        return 0

    if args.cmd == "validate":
        import conductor_authority as CA
        if args.delegated or args.judge_verdict:
            if args.owner_said or args.by_card or args.per_ruling:
                print("REFUSED: --delegated is the route WITHOUT his authority; "
                      "do not combine it with --owner-said, --by-card or --per-ruling",
                      file=sys.stderr)
                return 2
            return _validate(args.mod, None, delegated=True,
                             judge_verdict=args.judge_verdict)
        return _validate(args.mod, ("BY CARD: " + args.by_card if args.by_card and not args.owner_said else None)
                         or CA.words(args.owner_said, args.per_ruling, args.why))

    if args.cmd == "review":
        import conductor_authority as CA
        import status
        said = CA.words(args.owner_said, args.per_ruling, args.why)
        if not said:
            print("refused: review needs --owner-said with his words or a Conductor instruction (%s)" % CA.ROUTE,
                  file=sys.stderr)
            return 2
        entry = status.record_owner_review(args.mod, said,
                                          run_id=args.run_id)
        print("%s: owner review recorded against run %s -> %s"
              % (args.mod, entry["owner_review"]["run_id"], entry["status"]))
        return 0

    if args.cmd == "run":
        import runner
        if args.policy != "abort" and not args.situational:
            # MODCHECK_POLICY_FIX_RECORD_NEEDS_SITUATIONAL: only the situational Watch reads --policy; run4 was
            # launched `--policy record` without it and the policy was silently never read.
            print("REFUSED: --policy %s is read only by the situational envelope; add --situational or drop "
                  "--policy" % args.policy)
            return 2
        if args.changed is not None:
            import targeting
            if len(args.mods) != 1:
                print("REFUSED: --changed suggests chains for one mod")
                return 2
            try:
                mod_dir = runner.find_mod_dir(args.mods[0])
                suite = runner.load_validation(mod_dir)
                res = targeting.changed(suite, targeting.changed_files(mod_dir, args.changed), mod_dir)
            except (targeting.TargetError, RuntimeError) as ex:
                print("REFUSED: %s" % ex)
                return 2
            for line in targeting.changed_report(res):
                print(line)
            return 0
        if args.drivers is not None:
            import drivers  # noqa: E402
            os.environ[drivers.ENV] = "1" if args.drivers == "on" else "0"
        if args.reuse is not None:
            os.environ["MODCHECK_REUSE"] = {"off": "0", "report": "report", "on": "1"}[args.reuse]
        if args.gate is not None:
            os.environ["MODCHECK_GATE"] = args.gate
        if args.purpose is not None:
            os.environ["MODCHECK_PURPOSE"] = args.purpose
        elif args.full and not os.environ.get("MODCHECK_PURPOSE"):
            os.environ["MODCHECK_PURPOSE"] = "sweep"   # a sweep bypasses the gate (plan section 3)
        overrides = dict(kv.split("=", 1) for kv in args.item if "=" in kv)
        target_items = [kv for kv in args.item if "=" not in kv]
        chains = [c.strip() for c in args.chains.split(",") if c.strip()]
        rows = [r.strip() for r in args.rows.split(",") if r.strip()]
        targeted = bool(chains or rows or target_items)
        if targeted and args.full:
            print("REFUSED: --full and a target (--chains/--rows/--item ITEM_ID) contradict each other")
            return 2
        if args.preview and args.full and len(args.mods) == 1:
            # a sweep's driver plan only: testq submit sizes the job's timeout from it (TESTQ_SIZING_FIX_...)
            import drivers  # noqa: E402
            import json as _json
            try:
                suite = runner.load_validation(runner.find_mod_dir(args.mods[0]))
            except RuntimeError as ex:
                print("REFUSED: %s" % ex)
                return 2
            print("EXPECTED_DRIVERS " + _json.dumps(drivers.need_s(suite, [n for n, _ in suite.chains])[1]))
            # TESTQ_SWEEP_FIX_DRIVERS_OVER_CAP: which chains each driver serves, so testq sweep can split the sweep
            print("EXPECTED_CHAINS " + _json.dumps([n for n, _ in suite.chains]))
            print("EXPECTED_DRIVER_CHAINS " + _json.dumps(
                {d["name"]: list(d.get("chains") or ()) for d in drivers.plan(suite, [n for n, _ in suite.chains])}))
            return 0
        if args.preview and not targeted:
            print("REFUSED: --preview previews a TARGETED run; name --chains, --rows or --item ITEM_ID")
            return 2
        if not targeted and not args.full:
            print("REFUSED: a live run is TARGETED (owner 2026-10-25, standing_rulings.md \"Live runs are "
                  "TARGETED\"): name what the change touches with --item ITEM_ID, --chains a,b or --rows r1,r2. "
                  "The whole suite is a scheduled sweep (at most daily): add --full for that.")
            return 2
        targets = {}
        if targeted:
            if len(args.mods) != 1 or len(target_items) > 1:
                print("REFUSED: a targeted run names one mod and at most one --item ITEM_ID")
                return 2
            import targeting
            mod = args.mods[0]
            try:
                suite = runner.load_validation(runner.find_mod_dir(mod))
                text = targeting.item_text(target_items[0]) if target_items else None
                sel = targeting.resolve(suite, chains, rows, target_items[0] if target_items else None, text)
            except (targeting.TargetError, RuntimeError) as ex:
                print("REFUSED: %s" % ex)
                return 2
            for line in targeting.preview(sel):     # the exact plan, per chain, before anything launches
                print(line)
            import json as _json                    # machine line: the worker marks planned rows that never ran NOT_RUN
            print("EXPECTED_ROWS " + _json.dumps(list(sel.get("rows_run", []))))
            import drivers  # noqa: E402            # the "pre" drivers --drivers on would start, with their timeouts
            print("EXPECTED_DRIVERS " + _json.dumps(drivers.need_s(suite, sel["chains"])[1]))
            if args.preview:
                return 0
            targets[mod] = sel
            if target_items and mod not in overrides:
                overrides[mod] = target_items[0]
        mods = [(m, overrides.get(m, "MODCHECK_%s_RUN_1" % m.upper()))
               for m in args.mods]
        results = runner.run(mods, debug=args.debug, dry_run=args.dry_run,
                             situational=args.situational, policy=args.policy,
                             targets=targets, seat=args.seat, canary=args.canary, validity=args.validity)
        bad = [m for m, r in results.items() if not r["all_green"]]
        for m, r in results.items():
            print("%-20s %s" % (m, _verdict_line(r)))
        return 1 if bad else 0

    return 2


def _verdict_line(result):
    """One line per mod. Names WHICH half failed, because "RED" alone sent the
    pit's real defect -- right state, absent appearance -- unnamed for a month."""
    if result.get("refused"):
        return "REFUSED  %s" % result["refused"]
    tg = result.get("targeted")
    if tg:      # never a bare GREEN/RED for a subset: it would read as the full-suite verdict
        scope = "TARGETED %d/%d chains (%s)" % (len(tg["chains"]), tg.get("of_chains", 0), ",".join(tg["chains"]))
        return scope + " " + _verdict_line(dict(result, targeted=None))
    if result["all_green"]:
        return "GREEN"
    failed = []
    if not result.get("state_all_green", result["all_green"]):
        failed.append("state")
    if result.get("visual") and not result.get("visual_all_green"):
        failed.append("judge: %s" % ", ".join(
            "%s=%s" % (v["id"], v["verdict"])
            for v in result["visual"] if not v["pass"]))
    return "RED" + ("  (%s)" % "; ".join(failed) if failed else "")


DELEGATED_VERDICTS = ("PASS", "KEEP", "APPROVE", "YES")


def _judge_verdict_ok(root, path):
    """(relpath, None) when PATH is a committed-style judge verdict that passes,
    else (None, why). delegation_policy.md §3: verdicts live under
    infrastructure/state/delegated/<date>/ and are cited by path."""
    import json
    if not path:
        return None, "--delegated needs --judge-verdict <path to the judge's verdict JSON>"
    full = path if os.path.isabs(path) else os.path.join(root, path)
    full = os.path.realpath(full)
    base = os.path.realpath(os.path.join(root, "infrastructure", "state", "delegated"))
    if not full.startswith(base + os.sep):
        return None, "judge verdict must live under infrastructure/state/delegated/ (got %s)" % path
    if not os.path.isfile(full):
        return None, "judge verdict file not found: %s" % path
    try:
        with open(full, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            data = json.load(fh)
    except ValueError as e:
        return None, "judge verdict is not JSON (%s): %s" % (e, path)
    verdict = str(data.get("verdict", "")).strip().upper() if isinstance(data, dict) else ""
    if verdict not in DELEGATED_VERDICTS:
        return None, ("judge verdict is %r, not one of %s: %s"
                      % (verdict or "missing", "/".join(DELEGATED_VERDICTS), path))
    return os.path.relpath(full, os.path.realpath(root)).replace(os.sep, "/"), None


def _validate(mod, owner_said, delegated=False, judge_verdict=None):
    """Print the must-show lines about to BIND, then record his validation.

    Refuses to bless silently, exactly as `code_review_status.py mark-clean`
    does: with no `--owner-said` this prints the bar and writes nothing, so the
    lines can be read to him first. That is the whole point of the verb -- an
    agent-drafted checklist becomes a bar only on his word (owner, 2026-09-15:
    'I write vision, agent writes checklist, I validate checklist').
    """
    import northstar
    import runner
    walk = northstar.find_walk(runner.ROOT, mod)
    if not walk:
        print("REFUSED: %s has no validation walk under design/validation_walks/"
              % mod)
        return 2
    ns = northstar.parse(walk)
    if not ns["present"]:
        print("REFUSED: %s has no `## north star` section -- there is nothing "
              "to validate.\n  %s" % (mod, walk))
        return 2

    print("%s — %s" % (mod, walk))
    print("state on disk: %s%s" % (ns["state"],
                                   "" if not ns["reason"] else "  (%s)" % ns["reason"]))

    # A present-but-misformatted section parses to zero bars, and validating
    # that writes VALIDATED against an empty checklist: `bar_for()` then returns
    # nothing, the visual floor finds nothing uncovered, and the mod silently
    # STOPS being refused. Refusing here is the only thing standing between a
    # formatting slip and a validation that means nothing. Both lists empty is
    # the refusal; must-show empty with cannot-show present is a legitimate
    # walk that only forbids things.
    if not ns["must_show"] and not ns["cannot_show"]:
        print("\nREFUSED: the `## north star` section parses to ZERO bars, so "
              "validating it would\nrecord an approval that binds nothing and "
              "silently stops %s being refused." % mod)
        print("  Expected line format:  - [ ] `some_bar_id` — what must be "
              "visible")
        print("  under a `### must show` or `### cannot show` subheading.")
        print("  Copy the shape from a walk that parses: "
              "design/validation_walks/RimMandrake/FlowWorks.md")
        print("  %s" % walk)
        return 2

    print("\nThese lines BIND once validated. Every one of them refuses the mod "
          "until some\ncomponent claims it with `shows=`, and is then judged "
          "against a screenshot:\n")
    for req_id in ns["must_show"]:
        print("  must    %-32s %s" % (req_id, ns["must_show_text"][req_id]))
    for req_id in ns["cannot_show"]:
        print("  cannot  %-32s %s" % (req_id, ns["cannot_show_text"][req_id]))

    if delegated:
        rel, why = _judge_verdict_ok(runner.ROOT, judge_verdict)
        if not rel:
            print("\nREFUSED: %s" % why)
            return 2
        try:
            base, where = northstar.validated_baseline(walk)
        except ValueError as e:
            print("\nREFUSED: %s" % e)
            return 2
        with open(walk, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            now = northstar._section_lines(fh.read())
        loose = northstar.loosenings(base, now)
        if loose:
            print("\nREFUSED: the delegated route binds NEW bars only; against the "
                  "last validated section (%s) this loosens:" % where)
            for row in loose:
                print("  - %s" % row)
            print("Loosening a bar (remove, merge, relax) stays his "
                  "(delegation_policy.md §2.1): use --owner-said.")
            return 2
        owner_said = "%s; judge verdict %s%s" % (
            northstar.DELEGATED_WHY, rel,
            "" if base is None else "; additions only vs %s" % where[:12])
        print("\ndelegated: %s" % ("no earlier validated section -- every bar is new"
                                    if base is None else
                                    "additions only vs the validated section at %s" % where[:12]))

    if not owner_said:
        print("\n%d must-show + %d cannot-show lines would bind %s."
              % (len(ns["must_show"]), len(ns["cannot_show"]), mod))
        print("Nothing written. Read these to him; then re-run with "
              "--owner-said \"<his verbatim words>\", or the Conductor's "
              "instruction with --per-ruling.")
        return 1

    written = northstar.record_validation(walk, owner_said)
    print("\nVALIDATED at %s\n  %s: %s" % (written[:12], "authority" if delegated else "owner said",
                                            owner_said))
    if delegated:
        print("  Record it: rimflow note <ITEM> --why \"%s\" --text \"<mod> bound; %s\"; "
              "commit body line 'Delegated: new north-star bars — <mod>'."
              % (northstar.DELEGATED_WHY, judge_verdict))
    print("  %d must-show + %d cannot-show lines now bind %s."
          % (len(ns["must_show"]), len(ns["cannot_show"]), mod))
    print("  Any later edit to the section reverts it to DRAFT by hash "
          "mismatch.")
    return 0


def _mod_dir_or_die(mod):
    import runner
    return runner.find_mod_dir(mod)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""row_verdict.py -- read ONE modcheck run's results JSON and say whether named rows hold (ACC_BIOMES_FIXES_LIVE_RERUN_1).

    python3 src/RimMandrake/Utils/modcheck/live_queue/row_verdict.py --mod Miasma --max-age-min 30 \
        --row returning_a_young_wins_her_tolerance --unmeasured-ok "no warden mother and no water cell"

It only READS the newest Transient/modcheck/<Mod>_<stamp>.json (runner.write_sheet); the live half is the
`modcheck/cli.py run <Mod> --chains ...` call before it on the same live-proof line.

  --row NAME          a component that must read verdict PASS (repeatable). `~TEXT` matches the one component whose
                      name contains TEXT (exactly one, or it is a FAIL of the reader: an ambiguous row is never a pass).
  --unmeasured-ok RX  an UNMEASURED row whose detail matches RX counts as holding (a site fact the criterion allows).
  --max-age-min N     the newest run must be younger than N minutes (a stale run is not this sitting's evidence).

Exit 0 = every row holds; 1 = a row is missing, FAIL, UNMEASURED (not allowed), NOT_RUN, or the run is stale/absent.
judge() is pure; `--selftest` exercises it offline.
"""
import argparse
import glob
import json
import os
import re
import sys
import time

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
ROOT = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(HERE, "..", "..", "..", "..", ".."))
SHEET_DIR = os.path.join(ROOT, "Transient", "modcheck")


def components(data):
    return [c for ch in ((data or {}).get("summary") or {}).get("chains") or [] for c in ch.get("components") or []]


def find(comps, row):
    if row.startswith("~"):
        hits = [c for c in comps if row[1:] in str(c.get("name", ""))]
    else:
        hits = [c for c in comps if c.get("name") == row]
    return hits


def judge(data, rows, unmeasured_ok=None):
    """-> (ok, [one line per row])."""
    comps = components(data)
    ok, lines = True, []
    for row in rows:
        hits = find(comps, row)
        if len(hits) != 1:
            ok = False
            lines.append("%s: %d matching rows (want exactly 1)" % (row, len(hits)))
            continue
        c = hits[0]
        v, detail = str(c.get("verdict")), str(c.get("detail") or "")
        held = v == "PASS" or (v == "UNMEASURED" and unmeasured_ok and re.search(unmeasured_ok, detail))
        ok = ok and bool(held)
        lines.append("%s: %s%s%s" % (c.get("name"), v, " (allowed)" if held and v != "PASS" else "",
                                     (" -- " + detail[:200]) if detail else ""))
    return ok, lines


def newest(sheet_dir, mod):
    runs = sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(sheet_dir, "%s_*.json" % mod)), key=os.path.getmtime)
    return runs[-1] if runs else None


def check(sheet_dir, mod, rows, max_age_min, unmeasured_ok=None):
    path = newest(sheet_dir, mod)
    if not path:
        return 1, ["no %s run JSON in %s" % (mod, sheet_dir)]
    age = (time.time() - os.path.getmtime(path)) / 60.0
    if age > max_age_min:
        return 1, ["newest run %s is %.0f min old (> %d): rerun the live half" % (path, age, max_age_min)]
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        data = json.load(f)
    if data.get("mod") != mod:
        return 1, ["%s names mod %r, not %r" % (path, data.get("mod"), mod)]
    ok, lines = judge(data, rows, unmeasured_ok)
    return (0 if ok else 1), ["run %s" % path] + lines


def selftest():
    def d(*comps):
        return {"mod": "M", "summary": {"chains": [{"name": "c", "components": list(comps)}]}}
    P = {"name": "a_round_trips", "verdict": "PASS"}
    F = {"name": "b", "verdict": "FAIL", "detail": "x"}
    U = {"name": "u", "verdict": "UNMEASURED", "detail": "ERROR no warden mother and no water cell on map"}
    U2 = {"name": "u", "verdict": "UNMEASURED", "detail": "bridge timed out"}
    cases = [
        (d(P), ["a_round_trips"], None, True),
        (d(P), ["missing"], None, False),
        (d(F), ["b"], None, False),
        (d(U), ["u"], None, False),                                  # UNMEASURED is not PASS by default
        (d(U), ["u"], "no warden mother and no water cell", True),
        (d(U2), ["u"], "no warden mother and no water cell", False),  # an UNMEASURED of another cause is not allowed
        (d(P, F), ["a_round_trips", "b"], None, False),
        (d(P), ["~round_trips"], None, True),
        (d(P, dict(P, name="z_round_trips")), ["~round_trips"], None, False),   # ambiguous substring
        (d({"name": "n", "verdict": "NOT_RUN"}), ["n"], None, False),
        ({}, ["a"], None, False),
    ]
    bad = 0
    for i, (data, rows, um, want) in enumerate(cases):
        got, lines = judge(data, rows, um)
        if got != want:
            bad += 1
            print("case %d: want %s got %s %s" % (i, want, got, lines))
    print("row_verdict selftest: %s (%d cases)" % ("PASS" if not bad else "FAIL", len(cases)))
    return 1 if bad else 0


def main(argv=None):
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n")[0])
    ap.add_argument("--mod")
    ap.add_argument("--row", action="append", default=[])
    ap.add_argument("--unmeasured-ok")
    ap.add_argument("--max-age-min", type=int, default=30)
    ap.add_argument("--dir", default=SHEET_DIR)
    ap.add_argument("--selftest", action="store_true")
    a = ap.parse_args(argv)
    if a.selftest:
        return selftest()
    if not a.mod or not a.row:
        ap.error("--mod and at least one --row are required")
    code, lines = check(a.dir, a.mod, a.row, a.max_age_min, a.unmeasured_ok)
    print(("PASS " if code == 0 else "FAIL ") + a.mod)
    for line in lines:
        print("  " + line)
    return code


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""live_log_check.py -- does the RUNNING game's Player.log name a token in an error line? Read-only, no bridge call.

    python3 src/RimMandrake/Utils/live_log_check.py --absent RUT_ExplosiveGrowthRoster --absent RUT_PaleMoss [--warnings]

For criteria worded "Player.log carries no error naming X" (RA_S09_LIVE_WIRE_ONE_REAL_LEAF). A line is an error line when
it matches ERROR_RE (with --warnings, WARN_RE too); a token is matched as a literal substring of such a line.

--never TOKEN fails on ANY line naming the token, error word or not. Player.log carries no level marker: a Log.Warning
is bare text (stack traces are off), so a warning without the word "warn" in it is invisible to --warnings. Name such a
message by its own text with --never ("[RM Minerals] quarry", "name only disabled mineables").

Exit 0 no error line names any token, 1 one does (a real FAIL; the lines are printed), 2 UNMEASURED: no running game,
a log older than the running game (it belongs to an earlier session), or a log without the anchor (default
"Bridge token:", printed once the load finished and RimBridge came up: a log before that has not seen the load's
errors yet). Pair it with live_def_check.py when the criterion also needs the mod to be loaded: an absent token in a
load that never had the mod is not a pass, and this file cannot tell.
"""
import argparse
import datetime
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
PASS, FAIL, UNMEASURED = 0, 1, 2
# Word-ended so an identifier is not an error: RUT_ErrorPlant and "0 errors" are not error lines, NullReferenceException,
# "2 errors" and "Config error in" are. The tokens and every underscore identifier are blanked out first (MASK_RE).
ERROR_RE = re.compile(r"errors?\b|exceptions?\b|\bfailed\b|\bcould not\b|\bcouldn't\b", re.I)
WARN_RE = re.compile(r"warn(ing)?s?\b", re.I)
NONE_RE = re.compile(r"\b(0|no|zero|without)\s+(errors?|exceptions?|warnings?)\b", re.I)
IDENT_RE = re.compile(r"\w*_\w*")
# A line that continues the record above it (a stack trace, an inner exception, a [Ref] stub), not a message of its
# own. Blank lines never split a record: "Exception:\n\n  defName: X" is one record. A failed patch prints its file on
# the next line, unindented ("file: C:\\...\\Patches\\X.xml"): without `file: ` a token naming the patch file was missed.
CONT_RE = re.compile(r"^(\s|at |file: |\(Filename|--- |Rethrow|\[0x|\[Ref |(Verse|RimWorld|UnityEngine|System|HarmonyLib|Mono)\.\S*[:(])")
ANCHOR = "Bridge token:"


def records(text):
    """-> [(first line number, [lines])]: a message line plus the continuation lines under it."""
    out = []
    for n, line in enumerate(text.splitlines(), 1):
        if not line.strip():
            continue
        if out and CONT_RE.match(line):
            out[-1][1].append(line)
        else:
            out.append((n, [line]))
    return out


def judge(text, tokens, warnings=False, anchor=ANCHOR, never=()):
    """-> (exit code, lines). Pure: `text` is the whole Player.log. A record (a message and its stack trace) fails when
    any of its lines is an error line (with `warnings`, a warning line too) and any of its lines names a token, as a
    literal substring: RUT_PaleMoss also hits RUT_PaleMossLarge, a false FAIL at worst, never a false PASS."""
    if anchor and anchor not in text:
        return UNMEASURED, ["UNMEASURED: the log has no %r yet: the load has not finished" % anchor]
    hits, recs = [], records(text)
    for n, lines in recs:
        named = [t for t in never if any(t in x for x in lines)]
        if named:
            hits.append("FAIL line %d names %s, which may never appear: %s" % (n, ", ".join(named),
                                                                              " | ".join(x.strip() for x in lines)[:240]))
    mask = re.compile("|".join(re.escape(t) for t in sorted(tokens, key=len, reverse=True)))

    def bad(line):
        line = NONE_RE.sub(" ", IDENT_RE.sub(" ", mask.sub(" ", line)))
        return ERROR_RE.search(line) or (warnings and WARN_RE.search(line))

    for n, lines in recs if tokens else ():
        named = [t for t in tokens if any(t in x for x in lines)]
        if named and any(bad(x) for x in lines):
            hits.append("FAIL line %d names %s: %s" % (n, ", ".join(named), " | ".join(x.strip() for x in lines)[:240]))
    if hits:
        return FAIL, hits[:40] + (["... %d more" % (len(hits) - 40)] if len(hits) > 40 else [])
    return PASS, (["PASS no %s line names %s" % ("error or warning" if warnings else "error", ", ".join(tokens))] if tokens
                  else []) + (["PASS no line names %s" % ", ".join(never)] if never else [])


def game_started():
    """The running RimWorld's start, epoch seconds to the millisecond; None when none or two run, or it cannot be read."""
    try:
        r = subprocess.run(["powershell.exe", "-NoProfile", "-Command",
                            "Get-Process RimWorldWin64 -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | ForEach-Object "
                            "{ $_.StartTime.ToUniversalTime().ToString('yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.fffZ') }"],
                           capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=60, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL)
        lines = [x.strip() for x in r.stdout.splitlines() if x.strip()]
        if len(lines) != 1:
            return None
        return datetime.datetime.strptime(lines[0], "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%fZ").replace(
            tzinfo=datetime.timezone.utc).timestamp()
    except (OSError, ValueError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired):
        return None


def main(argv=None):
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument("--absent", action="append", default=[], metavar="TOKEN")
    ap.add_argument("--never", action="append", default=[], metavar="TOKEN",
                    help="any line naming this fails, error word or not (a Log.Warning has no marker in Player.log)")
    ap.add_argument("--warnings", action="store_true", help="a warning line naming a token fails too")
    ap.add_argument("--log", default=None, help="another log (default: game_paths.PLAYER_LOG); skips the game check")
    a = ap.parse_args(argv)
    tokens = [t for t in (x.strip() for x in a.absent) if t]
    never = [t for t in (x.strip() for x in a.never) if t]
    if not tokens and not never:
        print("UNMEASURED: no token to look for")
        return UNMEASURED
    path = a.log
    if path is None:
        sys.path.insert(0, HERE)
        from game_paths import PLAYER_LOG as path
        started = game_started()
        if started is None:
            print("UNMEASURED: no running game")
            return UNMEASURED
        try:
            if os.path.getmtime(path) <= started:
                print("UNMEASURED: %s was last written before the running game started" % path)
                return UNMEASURED
        except OSError as e:
            print("UNMEASURED: %s" % e)
            return UNMEASURED
    try:
        with open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as f:
            text = f.read()
    except OSError as e:
        print("UNMEASURED: %s" % e)
        return UNMEASURED
    if a.log is None and game_started() != started:
        print("UNMEASURED: the running game changed while the log was read")
        return UNMEASURED
    code, lines = judge(text, tokens, a.warnings, never=never)
    print("\n".join(lines))
    print({PASS: "VERDICT PASS", FAIL: "VERDICT FAIL", UNMEASURED: "VERDICT UNMEASURED"}[code])
    return code


def safe_main(argv=None):
    """main(), where nothing may escape: an uncaught exception exits 1, which the runner would record as a FAIL."""
    try:
        return main(argv)
    except SystemExit:
        raise
    except BaseException as e:
        sys.stdout.write("UNMEASURED: " + ascii("%s: %s" % (type(e).__name__, str(e)[:200])) + "\n")

if __name__ == "__main__":

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""HORRORS_RAIDING_FACTION_1 live proof: the Assailant horrors reach the nightside and nowhere else.

    python.exe src/RimUtinni/UtinniPatches/prove_night_horrors_live.py A2 < /dev/null
    python.exe src/RimUtinni/UtinniPatches/prove_night_horrors_live.py A3 < /dev/null

Runs under WINDOWS python: RimBridge binds Windows loopback. Any loaded world serves: where it has no land in the wanted
band (a partial-coverage test world holds no nightside at all), the proof moves the LIVE PlanetGeometryDef's substellar
point per tile with RUT_HorrorSinkholeProbe.Geometry ("night <tile>" = the tile's antipode, arc 180; "day <tile>" = on
the tile, arc 0), prints the move, and restores the original point at the end ("restore").

  A2  on a freshly generated NIGHTSIDE player map (tile arc from the substellar point > nightsideBandMinArc + 5):
      at least one RUT_HorrorHive lair is on the map (the self-gating GenStep ran); the lair's RUT_HorrorSinkhole is a
      working door: RUT_HorrorSinkholeProbe.Descend (jawa/static_call) goes down it the player's way and the pocket map
      it opens is RUT_HorrorTunnels holding at least one hive, crysalis and mite larder and exactly one CaveExit (the
      probe then destroys that pocket map); and RUT_HorrorRaid, forced, fires and leaves pawns of the RUT_Horrors
      faction on the map.
  A3  on a freshly generated DAYSIDE player map (arc < terminatorBandMinArc - 5): no lair structure or crysalis of
      ours is on the map, and RUT_HorrorRaid, forced, reports canFireNow=false (dry run, nothing fires).

The arc uses the shipped geometry def (WeatherGeometryDefs_Ashkarr.xml) and the same formula as
RM_WeatherKernel.ArcDegrees, over the live world's own tile table (jawa/world_tile_export: tile indices belong to the
world that wrote them). Each run founds one player settlement, generates its map, and drops the map again at the end.
Exit 0 = the clause holds, 1 = it does not (or could not be measured)."""
import csv
import json
import math
import os
import random
import sys
import time
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
REPO = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(HERE, "..", "..", ".."))
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(REPO, "src", "RimMandrake", "Utils"))
GEOM = os.path.join(REPO, "src", "RimUtinni", "AshkarrWeatherSuite", "Defs", "WeatherGeometryDefs", "WeatherGeometryDefs_Ashkarr.xml")
LAIR = ["RUT_HorrorHive", "RUT_HorrorDen", "RUT_HorrorBurrow", "RUT_HorrorSinkhole", "RUT_HorrorMiteLarder",
        "RUT_HorrorCrysalis_Visceral", "RUT_HorrorCrysalis_Prowler", "RUT_HorrorCrysalis_Harvester", "RUT_HorrorCrysalis_Bulwark"]
FORMS = ["RM_Visceral", "RUT_HorrorBulwark", "RUT_HorrorHarvester", "RUT_HorrorProwler", "RUT_HorrorBroodLord"]
WATER = ("ocean", "lake", "sea", "water", "ice sheet")


class Game:
    def __init__(self):
        import rimbridge_client as rb
        host, port, token = rb.resolve_endpoint()
        self.s = rb.RimBridge(host=host, port=port, token=token, timeout=280.0)
        self.s.connect()

    def call(self, t, **p):
        r = self.s.call(t, p) or {}
        if isinstance(r, dict) and r.get("content"):
            try:
                r = json.loads(r["content"][0]["text"])
            except ValueError:
                pass
        return r


def geometry():
    g = ET.parse(GEOM).getroot().find(".//*[substellarLat]")
    return {k: float(g.findtext(k)) for k in ("substellarLat", "substellarLon", "terminatorBandMinArc", "nightsideBandMinArc")}


def arc(lat, lon, lat0, lon0):
    r = math.radians
    c = math.sin(r(lat0)) * math.sin(r(lat)) + math.cos(r(lat0)) * math.cos(r(lat)) * math.cos(r(lon - lon0))
    return math.degrees(math.acos(max(-1.0, min(1.0, c))))


def candidates(g, geo, night):
    exp = g.call("jawa/world_tile_export")
    path = exp.get("path") or exp.get("pathWritten") or ""
    if not path or not os.path.isfile(path):
        return None, "world_tile_export wrote no readable file: %s" % str(exp)[:300]
    out = []
    with open(path, newline="", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        for row in csv.DictReader(fh):
            b = (row.get("biome") or "").lower()
            if not b or any(w in b for w in WATER):
                continue
            a = arc(float(row["lat"]), float(row["long"]), geo["substellarLat"], geo["substellarLon"])
            if (night and a > geo["nightsideBandMinArc"] + 5) or (not night and a < geo["terminatorBandMinArc"] - 5):
                out.append((int(row["tile"]), round(a, 1), row.get("biome")))
    random.shuffle(out)
    return out, "%d %s land tiles in %s" % (len(out), "nightside" if night else "dayside", path)


def probe(g, method, args):
    r = g.call("jawa/static_call", type="RimMandrake.Utinni.UtinniPatches.RUT_HorrorSinkholeProbe", method=method, args=args)
    return str((r or {}).get("result", "")) or "no result: %r" % (r,)


def any_land(g):
    exp = g.call("jawa/world_tile_export")
    path = exp.get("path") or exp.get("pathWritten") or ""
    out = []
    if path and os.path.isfile(path):
        with open(path, newline="", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            for row in csv.DictReader(fh):
                b = (row.get("biome") or "").lower()
                if b and not any(w in b for w in WATER) and (row.get("hilliness") or "") != "Impassable":
                    out.append((int(row["tile"]), None, row.get("biome")))
    random.shuffle(out)
    return out


def make_map(g, tiles, shift=None):
    for tile, a, biome in tiles[:25]:
        if shift:
            moved = probe(g, "Geometry", "%s %d" % (shift, tile))
            print("geometry moved:", moved)
            want = "nightside=True" if shift == "night" else "nightside=False"
            if want not in moved or "tileArc=" not in moved:
                continue
            a = moved.split("tileArc=")[1].split()[0]
        f = g.call("jawa/colony_found", tile=tile, name="HorrorProbe")
        if not f.get("success"):
            continue
        m = g.call("jawa/world_tile_map_generate", tile=tile)
        if m.get("success") and m.get("mapId") is not None:
            g.call("jawa/set_current_map", mapId=m["mapId"])
            return {"tile": tile, "arc": a, "biome": biome, "mapId": m["mapId"], "mapIndex": m.get("mapIndex")}
    return None


def count(g, defs, pawns=False):
    r = g.call("jawa/list_things", defName=",".join(defs), includePawns=pawns, limit=500)
    things = r.get("things") or r.get("results") or []
    return things


def drop(g, m):
    info = g.call("jawa/map_info")
    if m and info.get("tile") == m["tile"] and m.get("mapIndex") is not None:
        g.call("jawa/map_drop", mapIndex=m["mapIndex"], notifyPlayer=False)


def run(clause):
    geo = geometry()
    g = Game()
    if g.call("rimworld/get_game_info").get("status") != "game_loaded":
        print("FAIL %s: no game loaded" % clause)
        return 1
    night = clause == "A2"
    tiles, note = candidates(g, geo, night)
    print(note)
    shift = None
    if tiles is None:
        print("FAIL %s: %s" % (clause, note))
        return 1
    if not tiles:
        # A test world may hold no land in the wanted band (a partial-coverage world: no nightside at all). Move the
        # live substellar point onto the tile ("day") or its antipode ("night") instead; restored in the finally.
        tiles = any_land(g)
        shift = "night" if night else "day"
        print("no %s land on this world: the proof moves the live substellar point per tile (%d land tiles)"
              % (shift, len(tiles)))
    m = None
    try:
        m = make_map(g, tiles, shift)
        if not m:
            print("FAIL %s: could not found+generate a map on any of %d candidate tiles" % (clause, min(25, len(tiles))))
            return 1
        return judge(g, clause, night, m)
    finally:
        drop(g, m)
        if shift:
            print("geometry restored:", probe(g, "Geometry", "restore"))


def judge(g, clause, night, m):
    print("map:", m)
    ok = False
    lair = count(g, LAIR)
    hives = [t for t in lair if t.get("def") == "RUT_HorrorHive"]
    if night:
        below = probe(g, "Descend", "go")
        kv = dict(x.split("=", 1) for x in below.split()[1:] if "=" in x)
        num = lambda k: int(kv.get(k, "-1")) if kv.get(k, "").lstrip("-").isdigit() else -1
        door = (below.startswith("descended ") and kv.get("pocket") == "True" and kv.get("generator") == "RUT_HorrorTunnels"
                and num("hives") >= 1 and num("crysalises") >= 1 and num("larders") >= 1 and num("exits") == 1)
        print("sinkhole descent: %s -> %s" % (below, "door works" if door else "DOOR BROKEN"))
        fire = g.call("jawa/fire_incident", incidentDef="RUT_HorrorRaid", forced=True)
        time.sleep(1)
        facs = g.call("jawa/list_factions", includeHidden=True, defName="RUT_Horrors")
        forms = [t for t in count(g, FORMS, pawns=True) if "Horror" in str(t.get("faction", "")) or "Assailant" in str(t.get("faction", ""))]
        print("lair things %d (hives %d); raid fired=%s canFireNow=%s blockedByDialog=%s; faction rows %s; Horror-faction forms on map %d"
              % (len(lair), len(hives), fire.get("fired"), fire.get("canFireNow"), fire.get("blockedByDialog"), str(facs)[:200], len(forms)))
        ok = door and len(hives) >= 1 and fire.get("canFireNow") is True and fire.get("success") is True and len(forms) >= 1
    else:
        dry = g.call("jawa/fire_incident", incidentDef="RUT_HorrorRaid", forced=True, dryRun=True)
        print("lair things %d; dry-run canFireNow=%s" % (len(lair), dry.get("canFireNow")))
        ok = len(lair) == 0 and dry.get("canFireNow") is False
    print(("PASS " if ok else "FAIL ") + clause)
    return 0 if ok else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    if len(sys.argv) != 2 or sys.argv[1] not in ("A2", "A3"):
        print(__doc__)
        sys.exit(1)
    sys.exit(run(sys.argv[1]))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""live_log_check.py -- does the RUNNING game's Player.log name a token in an error line? Read-only, no bridge call.

    python3 src/RimMandrake/Utils/live_log_check.py --absent RUT_ExplosiveGrowthRoster --absent RUT_PaleMoss [--warnings]

For criteria worded "Player.log carries no error naming X" (RA_S09_LIVE_WIRE_ONE_REAL_LEAF). A line is an error line when
it matches ERROR_RE (with --warnings, WARN_RE too); a token is matched as a literal substring of such a line.

--never TOKEN fails on ANY line naming the token, error word or not. Player.log carries no level marker: a Log.Warning
is bare text (stack traces are off), so a warning without the word "warn" in it is invisible to --warnings. Name such a
message by its own text with --never ("[RM Minerals] quarry", "name only disabled mineables").

Exit 0 no error line names any token, 1 one does (a real FAIL; the lines are printed), 2 UNMEASURED: no running game,
a log older than the running game (it belongs to an earlier session), or a log without the anchor (default
"Bridge token:", printed once the load finished and RimBridge came up: a log before that has not seen the load's
errors yet). Pair it with live_def_check.py when the criterion also needs the mod to be loaded: an absent token in a
load that never had the mod is not a pass, and this file cannot tell.
"""
import argparse
import datetime
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
PASS, FAIL, UNMEASURED = 0, 1, 2
# Word-ended so an identifier is not an error: RUT_ErrorPlant and "0 errors" are not error lines, NullReferenceException,
# "2 errors" and "Config error in" are. The tokens and every underscore identifier are blanked out first (MASK_RE).
ERROR_RE = re.compile(r"errors?\b|exceptions?\b|\bfailed\b|\bcould not\b|\bcouldn't\b", re.I)
WARN_RE = re.compile(r"warn(ing)?s?\b", re.I)
NONE_RE = re.compile(r"\b(0|no|zero|without)\s+(errors?|exceptions?|warnings?)\b", re.I)
IDENT_RE = re.compile(r"\w*_\w*")
# A line that continues the record above it (a stack trace, an inner exception, a [Ref] stub), not a message of its
# own. Blank lines never split a record: "Exception:\n\n  defName: X" is one record. A failed patch prints its file on
# the next line, unindented ("file: C:\\...\\Patches\\X.xml"): without `file: ` a token naming the patch file was missed.
CONT_RE = re.compile(r"^(\s|at |file: |\(Filename|--- |Rethrow|\[0x|\[Ref |(Verse|RimWorld|UnityEngine|System|HarmonyLib|Mono)\.\S*[:(])")
ANCHOR = "Bridge token:"


def records(text):
    """-> [(first line number, [lines])]: a message line plus the continuation lines under it."""
    out = []
    for n, line in enumerate(text.splitlines(), 1):
        if not line.strip():
            continue
        if out and CONT_RE.match(line):
            out[-1][1].append(line)
        else:
            out.append((n, [line]))
    return out


def judge(text, tokens, warnings=False, anchor=ANCHOR, never=()):
    """-> (exit code, lines). Pure: `text` is the whole Player.log. A record (a message and its stack trace) fails when
    any of its lines is an error line (with `warnings`, a warning line too) and any of its lines names a token, as a
    literal substring: RUT_PaleMoss also hits RUT_PaleMossLarge, a false FAIL at worst, never a false PASS."""
    if anchor and anchor not in text:
        return UNMEASURED, ["UNMEASURED: the log has no %r yet: the load has not finished" % anchor]
    hits, recs = [], records(text)
    for n, lines in recs:
        named = [t for t in never if any(t in x for x in lines)]
        if named:
            hits.append("FAIL line %d names %s, which may never appear: %s" % (n, ", ".join(named),
                                                                              " | ".join(x.strip() for x in lines)[:240]))
    mask = re.compile("|".join(re.escape(t) for t in sorted(tokens, key=len, reverse=True)))

    def bad(line):
        line = NONE_RE.sub(" ", IDENT_RE.sub(" ", mask.sub(" ", line)))
        return ERROR_RE.search(line) or (warnings and WARN_RE.search(line))

    for n, lines in recs if tokens else ():
        named = [t for t in tokens if any(t in x for x in lines)]
        if named and any(bad(x) for x in lines):
            hits.append("FAIL line %d names %s: %s" % (n, ", ".join(named), " | ".join(x.strip() for x in lines)[:240]))
    if hits:
        return FAIL, hits[:40] + (["... %d more" % (len(hits) - 40)] if len(hits) > 40 else [])
    return PASS, (["PASS no %s line names %s" % ("error or warning" if warnings else "error", ", ".join(tokens))] if tokens
                  else []) + (["PASS no line names %s" % ", ".join(never)] if never else [])


def game_started():
    """The running RimWorld's start, epoch seconds to the millisecond; None when none or two run, or it cannot be read."""
    try:
        r = subprocess.run(["powershell.exe", "-NoProfile", "-Command",
                            "Get-Process RimWorldWin64 -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | ForEach-Object "
                            "{ $_.StartTime.ToUniversalTime().ToString('yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.fffZ') }"],
                           capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=60, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL)
        lines = [x.strip() for x in r.stdout.splitlines() if x.strip()]
        if len(lines) != 1:
            return None
        return datetime.datetime.strptime(lines[0], "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%fZ").replace(
            tzinfo=datetime.timezone.utc).timestamp()
    except (OSError, ValueError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired):
        return None


def main(argv=None):
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument("--absent", action="append", default=[], metavar="TOKEN")
    ap.add_argument("--never", action="append", default=[], metavar="TOKEN",
                    help="any line naming this fails, error word or not (a Log.Warning has no marker in Player.log)")
    ap.add_argument("--warnings", action="store_true", help="a warning line naming a token fails too")
    ap.add_argument("--log", default=None, help="another log (default: game_paths.PLAYER_LOG); skips the game check")
    a = ap.parse_args(argv)
    tokens = [t for t in (x.strip() for x in a.absent) if t]
    never = [t for t in (x.strip() for x in a.never) if t]
    if not tokens and not never:
        print("UNMEASURED: no token to look for")
        return UNMEASURED
    path = a.log
    if path is None:
        sys.path.insert(0, HERE)
        from game_paths import PLAYER_LOG as path
        started = game_started()
        if started is None:
            print("UNMEASURED: no running game")
            return UNMEASURED
        try:
            if os.path.getmtime(path) <= started:
                print("UNMEASURED: %s was last written before the running game started" % path)
                return UNMEASURED
        except OSError as e:
            print("UNMEASURED: %s" % e)
            return UNMEASURED
    try:
        with open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as f:
            text = f.read()
    except OSError as e:
        print("UNMEASURED: %s" % e)
        return UNMEASURED
    if a.log is None and game_started() != started:
        print("UNMEASURED: the running game changed while the log was read")
        return UNMEASURED
    code, lines = judge(text, tokens, a.warnings, never=never)
    print("\n".join(lines))
    print({PASS: "VERDICT PASS", FAIL: "VERDICT FAIL", UNMEASURED: "VERDICT UNMEASURED"}[code])
    return code


def safe_main(argv=None):
    """main(), where nothing may escape: an uncaught exception exits 1, which the runner would record as a FAIL."""
    try:
        return main(argv)
    except SystemExit:
        raise
    except BaseException as e:
        sys.stdout.write("UNMEASURED: " + ascii("%s: %s" % (type(e).__name__, str(e)[:200])) + "\n")
        return UNMEASURED


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(safe_main())

"""taozin_nest_live.py - live clauses L2/L3 of TAOZIN_SPLIT_BUILD_ONE_WORM_BECOMES_TWO on a generated RM_Abyss map.

    python3 src/RimStarWars/SWBestiary/taozin_nest_live.py L2     # WSL: stages an Abyss map, re-runs under python.exe
    python3 src/RimStarWars/SWBestiary/taozin_nest_live.py L3     # same staging (reuses a current RM_Abyss map)
    python.exe ...\\taozin_nest_live.py --inner L2 --out <json>   # the bridge half (Windows side)

L2 (owner card 2026-10-17, "A map feature with a guarding adult"; Crags = RM_Abyss): map generation on RM_Abyss runs
RSW_GenStep_TaozinNest (patched onto RM_Abyss.extraGenSteps), so the fresh map holds GRUB_MIN..GRUB_MAX living
RSW_TaozinGrub (the grub is never wild, so every one is the nest's), SILK_MIN..SILK_MAX stacks of RSW_WoolTaozin, every
grub and stack within NEST_RADIUS of the grubs' centre, and a living unowned RSW_Taozin within GUARD_RADIUS of it.
A patch that matches nothing, a GenStep that never runs or a gate that skips the map reads 0 grubs: FAIL.
L3 (the art reads in game): every nest grub and the guarding adult has thing_explain appearance rows whose body texPath
is the shipped one (EXPECTED_BODY, pinned to the defs by selftest_taozin_nest_live.py) and is held by >= 1 running
pack. Held by none = the renderer draws BadTex: FAIL.

Staging: a FRESH scratch vanilla quicktest world, a 2-ring land patch re-tiled to RM_Abyss with the Abyss's measured tile
values (design/Jawa/worldbuilding/biomes/abyss.md section 0: temp median -10.5 C, elevation median 490 m, the hilliest
def, LargeHills), centre mutators stripped, colony_found + world_tile_map_generate, map made current. Recipe:
Utils/modcheck/biome_site.py, as GelatinousSlime/live_kit_art.py uses it. Never Ash'karr, never a world a player
receives (CLAUDE.md worldgen ban); nothing is saved. If the CURRENT map is already RM_Abyss it is read instead (one
staging serves both lines in a sitting).
Exit 0 holds, 1 the clause is false, 2 UNMEASURED (no bridge, wrong load, wrong map, unreadable read). Callers hold the
bridge lock; this never takes it.
"""
import json
import math
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import time
import types

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
REPO = os.path.normpath(os.path.join(HERE, "..", "..", ".."))
UTILS = os.path.join(REPO, "src", "RimMandrake", "Utils")
MODCHECK = os.path.join(UTILS, "modcheck")
SCRATCH = "/mnt/d/ClaudeWork/rimmandrake/scratch/taozin_nest"
TIMEOUT = 530
BIOME = "RM_Abyss"
ADULT, GRUB, SILK = "RSW_Taozin", "RSW_TaozinGrub", "RSW_WoolTaozin"
GRUB_MIN, GRUB_MAX = 2, 4          # RSW_TaozinNest.xml RM_CaveElement_Pawns count 2~4
SILK_MIN, SILK_MAX = 2, 3          # RM_CaveElement_Things stacks 2~3
NEST_RADIUS = 10.0                 # cave elements fall back to cells within ~4 of the site; 10 leaves slack
GUARD_RADIUS = 14.0                # the anchored adult spawns at the site; a 10-cell body may stand off it
EXPECTED_BODY = {ADULT: "Things/Pawn/Animal/RSW_Taozin/RSW_Taozin",
                 GRUB: "Things/Pawn/Animal/RSW_TaozinGrub/RSW_TaozinGrub"}
SPEC = types.SimpleNamespace(       # the fields biome_site.choose_tile / retile read
    BIOME=BIOME, LAT_MAX=45.0, MAP_SIZE=200,
    TILE={"temperature": -10.5, "rainfall": 0.0, "elevation": 490.0, "hilliness": "LargeHills", "swampiness": 0.0})


def pos(t):
    p = t.get("position") or {}
    return float(p.get("x")), float(p.get("z"))


def alive(t):
    return not t.get("dead")


def unowned(t):
    return t.get("faction") in (None, "", "None") and t.get("factionName") in (None, "")


def nest(things):
    """(rc, lines, ids) for L2 from list_things rows (includePawns) of ADULT, GRUB and SILK. Pure, for the selftest."""
    grubs = [t for t in things if t.get("def") == GRUB and alive(t)]
    silk = [t for t in things if t.get("def") == SILK]
    adults = [t for t in things if t.get("def") == ADULT and alive(t) and unowned(t)]
    lines = ["grubs %d, silk stacks %d, unowned adults %d" % (len(grubs), len(silk), len(adults))]
    fails = []
    if not (GRUB_MIN <= len(grubs) <= GRUB_MAX):
        fails.append("grubs %d, want %d..%d (0 = the nest never generated; more = a grub came from elsewhere)" % (
            len(grubs), GRUB_MIN, GRUB_MAX))
    if not (SILK_MIN <= len(silk) <= SILK_MAX):
        fails.append("silk stacks %d, want %d..%d" % (len(silk), SILK_MIN, SILK_MAX))
    guard = None
    if grubs:
        cx = sum(pos(t)[0] for t in grubs) / len(grubs)
        cz = sum(pos(t)[1] for t in grubs) / len(grubs)
        lines.append("nest centre %.1f,%.1f" % (cx, cz))
        for t in grubs + silk:
            d = math.hypot(pos(t)[0] - cx, pos(t)[1] - cz)
            if d > NEST_RADIUS:
                fails.append("%s %s %.1f cells from the nest (> %s)" % (t.get("def"), t.get("id"), d, NEST_RADIUS))
        near = sorted((math.hypot(pos(a)[0] - cx, pos(a)[1] - cz), a.get("id")) for a in adults)
        if near and near[0][0] <= GUARD_RADIUS:
            guard = near[0][1]
            lines.append("guard %s at %.1f cells" % (guard, near[0][0]))
        else:
            fails.append("no unowned living %s within %s of the nest (nearest %s)" % (
                ADULT, GUARD_RADIUS, "%.1f" % near[0][0] if near else "none"))
    lines += ["FAIL " + f for f in fails]
    ids = [t.get("id") for t in grubs] + ([guard] if guard else [])
    return (1 if fails else 0), lines + ([] if fails else ["HOLDS"]), ids


def art(ids, defs_by_id, explain):
    """(rc, lines) for L3: each nest pawn's appearance body row is EXPECTED_BODY[def] and held by a running pack."""
    if not ids or not any(defs_by_id.get(i) == ADULT for i in ids) or not any(defs_by_id.get(i) == GRUB for i in ids):
        return 2, ["UNMEASURED: no nest adult and grub to read (L2 must hold first): %s" % ids]
    fails, blind = [], []
    for pid in ids:
        name = defs_by_id.get(pid)
        ex = explain(pid) or {}
        app = ex.get("appearance") or {}
        rows = app.get("paths") if isinstance(app, dict) else None
        if ex.get("success") is False or not rows:
            blind.append("%s %s appearance unread: %s" % (name, pid, str(ex)[:150]))
            continue
        body = [r for r in rows if r.get("role") == "body"]
        if not body:
            fails.append("%s %s has no body row: %s" % (name, pid, rows))
            continue
        for r in body:
            if r.get("texPath") != EXPECTED_BODY[name]:
                fails.append("%s %s body texPath %s, want %s" % (name, pid, r.get("texPath"), EXPECTED_BODY[name]))
            elif not r.get("packsHoldingPath"):
                fails.append("%s %s body %s is held by no running pack: draws BadTex" % (name, pid, r.get("texPath")))
    lines = ["pawns explained %d" % len(ids)] + ["FAIL " + f for f in fails]
    if fails:
        return 1, lines
    if blind:
        return 2, lines + ["UNMEASURED: " + b for b in blind]
    return 0, lines + ["HOLDS"]


def stage(s, rec, work):
    import biome_site as B
    NS = B.pyre()
    mods, retired = B.running_retired(s.call)
    lack = B.missing_dlc(mods)
    if retired or lack:
        raise B.SiteError("UNMEASURED: wrong load (retired %s, DLC missing %s)" % (retired, lack))
    rec["world"] = NS.fresh_quicktest_world(s)
    rec["colonyTile"] = s.call("jawa/map_info").get("tile")
    rec["pick"] = B.choose_tile(s, SPEC, work, rec["colonyTile"])
    centre = rec["pick"]["centre"]
    rec["retiled"] = B.retile(s, SPEC, rec["pick"]["patch"])
    NS.strip_mutators(s, centre)
    g = NS.generate(s, centre, SPEC.MAP_SIZE)   # raises on any failed mapgen finalize step
    rec["mapId"] = g["mapId"]
    s.call("jawa/set_current_map", mapId=g["mapId"])


def inner(clause, out_path):
    for p in (MODCHECK, UTILS):
        if p not in sys.path:
            sys.path.insert(0, p)
    from northstar_driver.session import FastSession
    rec = {"item": "TAOZIN_SPLIT_BUILD_ONE_WORM_BECOMES_TWO", "clause": clause,
           "utc": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", time.gmtime())}
    rc, lines = 2, ["UNMEASURED: did not reach the read"]
    try:
        with FastSession(strict=False, focus=False) as s:   # never focus the game (live-tier rule)
            mi = s.call("jawa/map_info")
            rec["staged"] = mi.get("mapBiome") != BIOME
            if rec["staged"]:
                stage(s, rec, os.path.join(os.path.dirname(out_path), "taozin_nest_site"))
                mi = s.call("jawa/map_info")
            rec["map"] = {k: mi.get(k) for k in ("mapId", "mapBiome", "tile", "sizeX", "sizeZ")}
            if mi.get("mapBiome") != BIOME or (rec.get("mapId") is not None and mi.get("mapId") != rec["mapId"]):
                raise RuntimeError("UNMEASURED: current map %s biome %s is not the %s map %s" % (
                    mi.get("mapId"), mi.get("mapBiome"), BIOME, rec.get("mapId")))
            r = s.call("jawa/list_things", defName=",".join((ADULT, GRUB, SILK)), includePawns=True, limit=5000) or {}
            if r.get("success") is False or not isinstance(r.get("things"), list) or r.get("isCompleteList") is False:
                raise RuntimeError("UNMEASURED: list_things unreadable or truncated: %s" % str(r)[:200])
            if not r.get("scanned"):
                raise RuntimeError("UNMEASURED: list_things scanned %r things: the read cannot see" % r.get("scanned"))
            things = r["things"]
            rec["things"] = things
            rc, lines, ids = nest(things)
            if clause == "L3":
                by_id = {t.get("id"): t.get("def") for t in things}
                rc, more = art(ids, by_id, lambda pid: s.call("jawa/thing_explain", id=pid))
                lines = lines + more
            rec["ids"] = ids
    except Exception as ex:   # every failure is UNMEASURED with its reason on disk, never a silent pass
        msg = str(ex)[:400]
        if rc != 1:
            rc, lines = 2, [msg if msg.startswith("UNMEASURED") else "UNMEASURED: %s: %s" % (type(ex).__name__, msg)]
    rec["rc"], rec["lines"] = rc, lines
    with open(out_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        json.dump(rec, fh, indent=1, sort_keys=True, default=str)
    print("%s: %s" % (clause, "\n".join(lines)))
    return rc


def win(path):
    out = subprocess.run(["wslpath", "-w", path], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=20).stdout.strip()
    if not out:
        raise SystemExit("wslpath gave nothing for %s" % path)
    return out


def outer(clause):
    os.makedirs(SCRATCH, exist_ok=True)
    out = os.path.join(SCRATCH, "%s_%d_%d.json" % (clause.lower(), os.getpid(), time.time_ns()))
    argv = ["python.exe", win(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "--inner", clause, "--out", win(out)]
    print("$ " + " ".join(argv), flush=True)
    try:
        rc = subprocess.run(argv, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, timeout=TIMEOUT).returncode
    except (OSError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired) as ex:
        print("UNMEASURED: bridge half did not finish: %s" % ex)
        return 2
    if not os.path.exists(out):
        print("UNMEASURED: the bridge half wrote no %s (exit %d)" % (out, rc))
        return 2
    with open(out, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        rec = json.load(fh)
    print("evidence: %s" % out)
    return rec.get("rc", 2) if rc in (0, 1, 2) and rc == rec.get("rc") else 2


def main(argv):
    clause = next((a for a in argv if a in ("L2", "L3")), None)
    if clause is None:
        print("usage: taozin_nest_live.py L2|L3")
        return 2
    if "--inner" in argv:
        out = argv[argv.index("--out") + 1] if "--out" in argv else os.path.join(os.getcwd(), "taozin_%s.json" % clause)
        return inner(clause, out)
    return outer(clause)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))
